\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-mode-ratio-jacobian-main}
\det D_\theta\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)\neq0.
\end{equation}
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Exact full common-core shell data at these same fixed settings remain
pinned to the single physical ratio target $C$. More precisely, for any
$\theta\in\Theta$ and any $\mathcal A>0$,
\[
\mathcal F_{\eta_*}(\theta,\mathcal A)=b
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta)=C.
\]
\item There are neighbourhoods $U\subset\Theta$ of $\theta_*$ and
$Y\subset(0,\infty)^2$ of $C$, together with a unique $C^1$ branch
\[
\mathcal I_{\eta_*}:Y\to U,\qquad \mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)=\theta_*,
\]
such that
\[
\mathcal R_*(\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(y))=y\qquad(y\in Y).
\]
If $\theta\in U$ and $\mathcal R_*(\theta)=y\in Y$, then
$\theta=\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(y)$.
\item If $\theta\in U$ and $\mathcal A>0$ satisfy
\[
\mathcal F_{\eta_*}(\theta,\mathcal A)=b,
\]
then necessarily
\[
\theta=\theta_*,
\qquad
\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta)=C.
\]
Consequently every nearby point $y\in Y\setminus\{C\}$ is only an abstract
ratio-space datum for the same fixed-setting inverse problem. It is not exact
full shell data at the fixed record $\eta_*$ and the same detector settings.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Part (i) is exactly the fixed-target consequence of
\Cref{lem:ratio-admissibility-main}: if
$\mathcal F_{\eta_*}(\theta,\mathcal A)=b$ for some $\mathcal A>0$, then
$\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta)=C$. The displayed exact shell identity at
$(\theta_*,\mathcal A_*)$ is part of the fixed-base-point setup recorded above,
so exact full common-core shell data at the fixed settings occur only at the
single physical ratio target $C$.

For the inverse branch in part (ii), the stated regularity makes
$\mathcal R_*:\Theta\to\RR^2$ a $C^1$ map with exact base point
$\mathcal R_*(\theta_*)=C$. To make the Jacobian condition explicit, write
\[
B_{\varphi,m}(\theta)=\beta_\infty(\theta)\Omega N(r_{\varphi,m};\theta),
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{mem},m}(\theta)=\beta_\infty(\theta)\Omega N(r_{{\mathrm{mem}},m};\theta).
\]
Then
\[
d_\theta R_m=
\frac{
e^{B_{\varphi,m}}\,d_\theta B_{\varphi,m}\,(e^{B_{\mathrm{mem},m}}-1)
-(e^{B_{\varphi,m}}-1)e^{B_{\mathrm{mem},m}}\,d_\theta B_{\mathrm{mem},m}
}
{(e^{B_{\mathrm{mem},m}}-1)^2}.
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:two-mode-ratio-jacobian-main} is the concrete requirement that
the two row covectors supplied by the two fixed-radius ratio equations are not
collinear at $\theta_*$. Apply the ordinary inverse function theorem to
$\mathcal R_*$ at $\theta_*$. This yields neighbourhoods $U,Y$ and the unique
$C^1$ inverse branch $\mathcal I_{\eta_*}$. Exterior admissibility of the fixed
record is an open condition in $\theta$, so $U$ may be shrunk if necessary to
keep the fixed radii in the allowed coordinate range throughout $U$.

For part (iii), combine part (i) with the uniqueness statement in part (ii).
If $\theta\in U$ and $\mathcal F_{\eta_*}(\theta,\mathcal A)=b$ for some
$\mathcal A>0$, then part (i) gives $\mathcal R_*(\theta)=C$, hence
$\theta=\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)=\theta_*$. The final sentence is just this local
uniqueness restated in the ratio-space variable: points
$y\in Y\setminus\{C\}$ parametrize nearby abstract ratio values, not nearby
exact fixed-target shell records.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Abstract calibrated toy-model corollary: delta-method transport for fixed-radius ratio estimates]\label{prop:two-mode-delta-main}
\ResponseStandingClause this statistical fixed-radius corollary starts only after
the deterministic inverse branch of \Cref{thm:two-mode-main} and the external
ratio-data CLT of \Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main} have both been supplied. It is
therefore a conditional delta-method transport statement for externally supplied
ratio data, not a corollary of the one-record regenerative CLT and not a
field-mediated communication construction of the kind studied in
\cite{KasprzakTjoa2025Transmission}. Let
$U$, $Y$, and $\mathcal I_{\eta_*}:Y\to U$ be the neighbourhoods and inverse
branch from \Cref{thm:two-mode-main}. Define
\[
\widehat\theta_N=
\begin{cases}
\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(\widehat y_N),& \widehat y_N\in Y,\\
\theta_*,& \widehat y_N\notin Y.
\end{cases}
\]
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item One has
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_*)
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\theta),
\]
with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:delta-covariance-main}
\Sigma_\theta
=D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)\,\Sigma_y\,D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)^\top
=\bigl[D_\theta\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)\bigr]^{-1}
\Sigma_y
\bigl[D_\theta\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)\bigr]^{-{\top}}.
\end{equation}
\item If $\widehat\Sigma_{y,N}\to\Sigma_y$ in probability and one sets
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{\theta,N}=
\begin{cases}
D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(\widehat y_N)\,
\widehat\Sigma_{y,N}\,
D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(\widehat y_N)^\top,& \widehat y_N\in Y,\\
0,& \widehat y_N\notin Y,
\end{cases}
\]
then
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{\theta,N}\to\Sigma_\theta
\qquad\text{in probability}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Because \Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main} gives
$\widehat y_N=C+O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2})$ and $Y$ is a neighbourhood of $C$,
\[
\mathbb P(\widehat y_N\in Y)\to1.
\]
Hence the auxiliary values assigned outside $Y$ are asymptotically negligible.
Apply the multivariate delta method to the $C^1$ map
$\mathcal I_{\eta_*}$ at the point $C$ using the external CLT from
\Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main}. This gives
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(\widehat y_N)-\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C))
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N\!\bigl(0,
D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)\Sigma_y D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)^\top\bigr).
\]
Since $\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)=\theta_*$, this is the stated Gaussian limit for
$\widehat\theta_N$. The identity
\[
D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(C)=\bigl[D_\theta\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)\bigr]^{-1}
\]
is the chain rule for the local inverse branch, yielding
\eqref{eq:delta-covariance-main}. Part (ii) follows from the continuity of
$D\mathcal I_{\eta_*}$ on $Y$, the convergence
$\widehat y_N\to C$ in probability, and Slutsky's theorem. No ratio-data
asymptotic is proved inside this corollary; all stochastic input comes from
\Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[One sufficient source of the ratio-data CLT]\label{rem:ratio-data-delta-source-main}
One standard route to \Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main} is external to the
fixed-setting long-record theorem: start from an
external estimator of the positive denominator vector
\[
D_*=(D_{\varphi,1}^*,D_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}^*,D_{\varphi,2}^*,D_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}^*)
\in(0,\infty)^4,
\]
for which
\[
C_1=\frac{D_{\varphi,1}^*}{D_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}^*},
\qquad
C_2=\frac{D_{\varphi,2}^*}{D_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}^*}.
\]
If an external procedure supplies estimators $\widehat D_N$ satisfying
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat D_N-D_*)\Longrightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_D),
\]
and one forms the ratio datum by
\[
\widehat y_N=G(\widehat D_N),\qquad
G(d_{\varphi,1},d_{{\mathrm{mem}},1},d_{\varphi,2},d_{{\mathrm{mem}},2})
=\left(\frac{d_{\varphi,1}}{d_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}},
\frac{d_{\varphi,2}}{d_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}}\right),
\]
then the multivariate delta method yields
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat y_N-C)\Longrightarrow \mathcal N(0,\Sigma_y),
\qquad
\Sigma_y=DG(D_*)\,\Sigma_D\,DG(D_*)^\top,
\]
with
\[
DG(D_*)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{1}{D_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}^*}
&
-\dfrac{D_{\varphi,1}^*}{(D_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}^*)^2}
& 0 & 0\\[1.1ex]
0 & 0 &
\dfrac{1}{D_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}^*}
&
-\dfrac{D_{\varphi,2}^*}{(D_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}^*)^2}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The same composition principle applies if one first proves a CLT for external
shell-location or lapse estimators and then passes to the denominators and
their quotients through the smooth maps in
\eqref{eq:two-mode-ratio-functions-main}. The present paper does not prove such
an external CLT; it records only the conditional inverse/sensitivity consequences once
that input is available. In particular,
\Cref{thm:one-record-estimates-main} already isolates why the single-record CLT
for $\gamma_2$ is insufficient for these ratio coordinates.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[External localization route to the ratio-data CLT]\label{prop:ratio-data-shell-source-main}
The same external input can arise from a localization protocol, but
that derivation is separate from, and not implied by, the one-record CLT proved in
\Cref{sec:records}. Keep the same fixed detector settings, the same exact
radius record $\eta_*\in J^4$, and the same background parameter
$\theta_*\in\Theta$ from \Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main}. Define the
fixed-parameter ratio map in the radius variables by
\[
h:\mathcal D\to(0,\infty)^2,
\qquad
h(\eta)=\mathcal R_\eta(\theta_*),
\]
on an open neighborhood $\mathcal D\subset J^4$ of $\eta_*$. Suppose an
external localization procedure supplies response-locus position estimators
$\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal D$ such that
\[
\sqrt N\,(\widehat\eta_N-\eta_*)
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\eta)
\]
for some positive semidefinite $4\times4$ matrix $\Sigma_\eta$. Then the
derived ratio datum
\[
\widehat y_N=h(\widehat\eta_N)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sqrt N\,(\widehat y_N-C)
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_y),
\qquad
\Sigma_y=
D_\eta h(\eta_*)\,\Sigma_\eta\,D_\eta h(\eta_*)^\top.
\]
Because $h(\eta_*)=\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)=C$, this is exactly one
sufficient protocol-level route to the external input assumed in
\Cref{ass:ratio-data-clt-main}. The present paper does not prove such a
localization CLT; it records only that, once supplied, the inverse-function
algebra of \Cref{prop:two-mode-delta-main} transports it to parameter space.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Inverse-branch meaning versus retuned exact targets]\label{rem:fixed-target-versus-retuned-main}
The interpretation of
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main,prop:two-mode-delta-main} is strictly fixed-setting.
Once the detector settings and the radius record $\eta_*$ are frozen, the ratio
target is the single point $C=(C_1,C_2)$ and the undivided shell target is the
single vector $b$. The deterministic corollary \Cref{thm:two-mode-main} says
that exact fixed-setting shell data at those same settings still occur only at
$y=C$, while the statistical corollary \Cref{prop:two-mode-delta-main} uses the
same inverse branch only for nearby observed denominator quotients $y$.

If one instead wants nearby $y$ to represent exact shell data, the detector
targets must vary with $y$. In the present notation the corresponding
$y$-dependent target vector is
\[
b(y)=
\left(
\log\varphi,\,
\frac{y_1\log\varphi}{\Delta\tau_1},\,
\log\varphi,\,
\frac{y_2\log\varphi}{\Delta\tau_2}
\right),
\]
because the exact within-mode quotient relation is
$y_m=\Delta\tau_m\Gamma_{{\mathrm{crit}},m}/\log\varphi$. The exact equation in
that retuned problem is then
\[
\mathcal F_{\eta_*}(\mathcal I_{\eta_*}(y),\mathcal A(y))=b(y),
\]
which is a different retuned-target calibration problem from the fixed-setting inverse problem
treated in \Cref{thm:two-mode-main,prop:two-mode-delta-main}.
\end{remark}

If one instead varies the radius quadruple as an ambient algebraic parameter,
the corresponding residual graph and the restriction to full common-core shell
data are recorded separately in
\Cref{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main,thm:full-shell-subset-main,cor:full-shell-restriction-main}. Those appendix statements describe the local geometry of the ratio residual equations in the enlarged data space; they are not local ratio-map inverse theorems from nearby shell records to background geometry.

Appendix~\ref{app:schwarzschild-toy} records a separate Schwarzschild toy
specialization of this fixed-radius algebra, including the one-parameter
Hartle--Hawking branch reduction and a worked table. It remains explicit
calibrated-model bookkeeping rather than an exact nonconstant-lapse
detector-field construction.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:jacobian-main}
The Jacobian condition~\eqref{eq:two-mode-ratio-jacobian-main} is the local regularity condition for the ratio-map inverse branch, evaluated at the exact radius record and physical ratio target. It can fail because the two modes produce redundant ratio functions, or because the chosen background parametrization affects the two recorded radii in linearly dependent ways. Equality $C_1=C_2$ is therefore not a complete degeneracy criterion; it is a warning sign that the two modes may not provide independent constraints. Choosing distinct sampling and recovery parameters is necessary in practice, but the determinant in~\eqref{eq:two-mode-ratio-jacobian-main} is the actual inverse-regularity test.
\end{remark}

\section{Short Parry Comparator}\label{sec:kms-shells}

\begin{remark}[Parry comparator and external calibration only]
\label{def:thermality-notions-main}
\label{prop:ideal-main}
\label{cor:conditional-calibration-bridge-main}
\label{thm:response-locus-main}
\label{ass:udw-rate-calibration-main}
This appendix is only a compact comparator, not part of the D-MAP theorem
package.  For the ideal one-step blanking comparison law
\[
P_\beta=
\begin{pmatrix}
p_\beta&1-p_\beta\\
1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad p_\beta=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},
\]
the standard golden-mean Parry calculation gives
\[
p_\beta=\varphi^{-1}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Gamma\Delta\tau=\log\varphi
\]
as the maximum-entropy benchmark on the golden-mean shift
\cite{Parry1964,LindMarcus1995}.  This comparison law is not the
sampled-boundary-reset D-MAP law used in Theorems~A--E.  If an external
positive \(C^1\) calibration \(R_\Omega:U\to(0,\infty)\) is supplied and a
rate is assigned by \(\Gamma=R_\Omega(x)\), the two scalar targets mentioned
in the paper correspond only to the inverse images
\[
R_\Omega^{-1}\!\left(\frac{\log\varphi}{\Delta\tau}\right),
\qquad
R_\Omega^{-1}\!\left(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}
(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)\right),
\]
with the usual regular-level-set interpretation where \(dR_\Omega\ne0\).
This is a response-side composition of externally supplied data with
record-selected constants.  It gives no inference from one visible D-MAP
record to \(R_\Omega\), \(\Gamma_+\), KMS temperature, lapse, coupling,
spectral weight, thermodynamic parameters, or ordered labelled rates.
\end{remark}

\section{Killed-reset fibres: an exact two-state arc and higher-state structure}

The minimal-realization statements in this subsection are recalled background,
not contributions of this paper.  Kalman's similarity theorem is the classical
source, and minimal MAP/phase-type formulations and canonical-coordinate
developments are given in
\cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP,
BladtNielsen2017MatrixExponential,MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical,
PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical}.  We state the consequence needed to locate
the visible fibre, classify the complete Markovian fibre of the physical
two-state kernel, and then prove the higher-state quantitative assertion: at a
minimal interior killed-reset kernel the admissible fibre has local dimension
\((n-1)^2\).  Nonunique MAP and Coxian representatives are documented in
\cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP,RizkBurkeWalsh2019CoxianNonuniqueness}.
Graph-specific time-to-event inverses are treated algebraically by
Radulescu et al.\ \cite{RadulescuEtAl2025TimeToEventIdentifiability}; the
criterion below instead isolates the exact orbit fibre for any declared
minimal killed-reset subclass.

\paragraph{Recalled minimal-realization uniqueness.}
Let \((a,A,b)\) and \((\widetilde a,\widetilde A,\widetilde b)\) be two real
scalar realizations of the same dimension \(n\) such that
\[
aA^k b=\widetilde a\widetilde A^k\widetilde b
\qquad(k\ge0).
\]
Assume that both reachability matrices
\[
[\,b,Ab,\ldots,A^{n-1}b\,],\qquad
[\,\widetilde b,\widetilde A\widetilde b,\ldots,
\widetilde A^{n-1}\widetilde b\,]
\]
and both observability matrices
\[
\begin{bmatrix}a\\aA\\\vdots\\aA^{n-1}\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde a\\\widetilde a\widetilde A\\\vdots\\
\widetilde a\widetilde A^{n-1}\end{bmatrix}
\]
have rank \(n\). Then there is a unique \(M\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\RR)\)
such that
\[
\widetilde a=aM,
\qquad \widetilde A=M^{-1}AM,
\qquad \widetilde b=M^{-1}b.
\]
These rank hypotheses are precisely properties \textup{(R)} and \textup{(L)}
of Bladt and Nielsen, whose Theorem~4.2.16 characterizes minimality by their
simultaneous validity; the corresponding intertwining relations are given in
their Lemmas~4.2.5--4.2.6
\cite[Theorem~4.2.16, p.~216, and Lemmas~4.2.5--4.2.6,
p.~212]{BladtNielsen2017MatrixExponential}. This standard result is invoked
here and is not claimed as a new theorem; see also Kalman
\cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems}, Telek--Horv\'ath
\cite{TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}, and
\cite{Ryden1996Aggregated,OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness,
OCinneide1991InvariantPolytopes}.

\begin{proposition}[Recalled orbit-fibre consequence of minimal realization]
\label{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main}
Fix \(n\ge2\), put \(\beta=e_n^\top\), and let
\[
\mathcal K_n=\{K\in\RR^{n\times n}:K\ge0,\ K\mathbf1\le\mathbf1,\
\operatorname{spr}(K)<1\}.
\]
For \(K\in\mathcal K_n\), define the killed-reset D-MAP by
\[
T_0=K,\qquad T_1=(I-K)\mathbf1\beta
\]
and its Palm survival coordinates by \(S_k(K)=\beta K^k\mathbf1\).
Call \(K\) minimal when both
\[
\mathcal C(K)=[\,\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1\,],
\qquad
\mathcal O(K)=
\begin{bmatrix}\beta\\ \beta K\\ \vdots\\ \beta K^{n-1}\end{bmatrix}
\]
have rank \(n\). Let
\[
\mathcal G_n=\{M\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\RR):
M\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ \beta M=\beta\},
\]
and let \(\mathfrak P_n\subset\mathcal G_n\) be the reset-preserving
permutation matrices.

For any declared subclass \(\mathcal C\subset\mathcal K_n\) of minimal
kernels, fix the structural equivalence \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) under which
identification is requested, and assume that \(K\sim_{\mathcal C}L\) implies
equality of visible laws. Examples are reset-preserving hidden-state
relabeling and, in a serial rate chart, permutation of the rate coordinates.
Define the Markovian orbit fibre
\[
\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=
\left\{M^{-1}KM\in\mathcal C:M\in\mathcal G_n\right\}
\big/\!\sim_{\mathcal C}.
\]
Then standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the following exact
characterization.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Two minimal kernels \(K,L\in\mathcal K_n\) generate the same stationary
visible click law if and only if
\[
\begin{aligned}
L&=M^{-1}KM &&\text{for the unique }M\in\mathcal G_n\\
&&&\text{implementing their normalized minimal realizations}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\item Equivalently, the declared hidden object is identifiable from the visible law within
\(\mathcal C\), modulo \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\), if and only if
\[
\#\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=1\qquad\text{for every }K\in\mathcal C.
\]
Pointwise identifiability at \(K\) is equivalent to the same condition at
that \(K\); if the cardinality exceeds one, its distinct classes are exactly
the hidden nonidentifiability fibre. Thus this assertion is the orbit-fibre
reformulation of part \textup{(i)}.
\end{enumerate}
Part~\textup{(ii)} is deliberately recorded only as terminology: after the
fibre has been defined, singleton fibre and identifiability modulo
\(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) are the same assertion.  Neither part is claimed as a
new realization theorem.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Deterministic reset makes the visible process renewal. Its Palm gap tail is
exactly \(S_k(K)\), so equality of visible stationary laws is equivalent to
equality of all the scalar coordinates \(\beta K^k\mathbf1\), \(k\ge0\).
Apply the minimal-realization theorem stated above to the triples
\((\beta,K,\mathbf1)\) and \((\beta,L,\mathbf1)\). Its hypotheses are exactly
the two displayed rank conditions in the proposition, and it gives a unique
similarity \(L=M^{-1}KM\). Preservation of the fixed input and output vectors
gives \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\beta M=\beta\), respectively.
Conversely, these two identities give
\[
\beta(M^{-1}KM)^k\mathbf1=\beta K^k\mathbf1
\]
for every \(k\), proving (i). Taking the intersection with
\(\mathcal C\) and then quotienting precisely the declared structural
equivalence proves
the necessary-and-sufficient assertion (ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put \(K=T_0\),
\(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), and
\[
 I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
\]
Then \(K\) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
\(\mathcal K_2\) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
\[
 \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
 \qquad
 K(q)=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
 bq & s+b(1-q)
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{F1}
\]
Here complete means that every \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same stationary
visible click law as \(K\) is \(K(q)\) for exactly one \(q\in I_\ast\).
Writing \(T_0(\alpha,\eta)\) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
rate \(\alpha\) and recovery rate \(\eta\), the endpoints are the two physical
triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
\[
 K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
 \qquad
 K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
 \tag{F2}
\]
If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every \(q\) strictly between the
endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then \(I_\ast=\{1\}\), so
the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First \(b>0\).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
the defining integral gives
\[
 b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
 \qquad
 b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
          =bq_\ast>0.
 \tag{F3}
\]
The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
\(p=s\), \(b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0\), and \(q_\ast=1\).  Consequently
\[
 \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
 \qquad
 \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
\]
so \(K\) is minimal.

Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
\[
 M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
\]
Multiplication, using \(b+s-p=bq_\ast\), gives
\(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)\) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since \(K\) is minimal, its scalar
Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same visible
law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
\(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)\) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
\(L\) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
forces every such \(L\) to have the displayed form.  If
\(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\), its lower-left entry
is \(bq\ge0\).  Invertibility excludes \(q=0\), hence \(q>0\).  Its
upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
\[
 \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
 \tag{F4}
\]

Conversely, let \(q\in I_\ast\).  The two diagonal entries in
\textup{(F1)} are affine in \(q\), with endpoint values \(p,s\) and \(s,p\),
respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
\(a=1-b-s>0\), the two killing deficits are
\[
 \mathbf1-K(q)\mathbf1
 =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
 \tag{F5}
\]
Similarity preserves the spectral radius
\(\max\{p,s\}<1\), so \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\).  This proves that the
displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
entry is \(bq\).

At \(q=1\) one recovers \(K\).  At \(q=q_\ast\),
\[
 K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that \(bq_\ast\) is precisely the no-click
recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
row has the same killing deficit \(a\); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
\(q_\ast\ne1\), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
inside \(I_\ast\) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
and both deficits are already strict there.  If \(q_\ast=1\),
\textup{(F4)} forces \(q=1\).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
identifiability statements follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-collision serial identifiability]
\label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates
\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed. Let
\[
Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
\]
with all other entries zero, and put
\[
T_0(\theta)=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
T_1(\theta)=(I-T_0(\theta))\mathbf1e_n^\top.
\]
Then the visible record identifies exactly the unordered rate multiset
\(\{\!\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\}\!\}\). Equivalently, the fibre of the
labelled serial parameter is its \(\mathfrak S_n\)-permutation orbit.

More explicitly, if the distinct rates are
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) with multiplicities
\(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the Palm tail
has the confluent Prony form
\[
S_k=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,\qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0,
\]
and its minimal recurrence polynomial is
\[
\chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
\]
The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
\((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible; hence
\(S_0,\ldots,S_{2n-1}\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), including all collision
multiplicities. Pole collision therefore changes conditioning and the local
root chart, but does not change population identifiability.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Starting in phase \(n\), the absorption time is
\(W=X_n+\cdots+X_1\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials with
rates \(\theta_i\). Its Laplace transform is
\[
\EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
=\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}{s}
\]
has at
\(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\). Partial-fraction inversion and
sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give the displayed exponential-polynomial form
with nonzero top confluent coefficient. Standard confluent Prony algebra
then gives the exact minimal annihilator \(\chi_\theta\)
\cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.

For completeness of the finite-coordinate assertion, the matrices
\(\mathcal O(Q)\) and \(\mathcal C(Q)\) are nonsingular: successive rows
\(e_n^\top Q^j\) and successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\) expose the nonzero
bidiagonal products triangularly. Because the exponential is injective on
the real spectrum of \(Q\), Hermite interpolation supplies a polynomial
\(p\) with \(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\); hence the corresponding observation and
reachability spaces for \(T_0=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are also full. Therefore
\[
(S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(T_0)\mathcal C(T_0)
\]
is invertible, and the first \(2n\) tails solve uniquely for the order-\(n\)
recurrence. The roots and their algebraic multiplicities recover
\(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\). Conversely, permuting
the independent summands does not change \(W\), the Palm gap law, or the
stationary renewal law. This proves the exact fibre claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative interior fibre dimension and positivity persistence]
\label{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}
For the unrestricted class with \(\sim_{\mathcal K_n}\) equal to
reset-preserving state relabelling, the hidden kernel is locally
nonidentifiable at every minimal interior point \(K\), where interior means
\(K>0\) and \((I-K)\mathbf1>0\) entrywise. More precisely, the
reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
\[
\mathfrak g_n=\{B:B\mathbf1=0,\ \beta B=0\},
\qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,
\]
and the orbit map
\[
\psi_K:\mathcal G_n\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{n\times n},\qquad
\psi_K(M)=M^{-1}KM,
\]
has injective differential
\[
D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\qquad(B\in\mathfrak g_n).
\]
Consequently the visible fibre through \(K\) contains, in a neighbourhood of
\(K\), a smooth immersed manifold of dimension exactly \((n-1)^2\).  Every
kernel on a sufficiently small neighbourhood of this orbit manifold remains
strictly substochastic: its entries and killing deficits are positive.  After
quotienting by the finite reset-preserving permutation group, the local fibre
still has dimension \((n-1)^2\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because \(\beta\mathbf1=1\),
\(\RR^n=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\oplus\ker\beta\).  Relative to this
decomposition, \(B\mathbf1=0\) removes the first block column and
\(\beta B=0\) forces the range into \(\ker\beta\).  Thus
\(B=\operatorname{diag}(0,A)\), with arbitrary
\(A\in\operatorname{End}(\ker\beta)\), and
\(\dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2\).

Differentiating \(\exp(-tB)K\exp(tB)\) at zero gives
\(D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\).  Suppose \([K,B]=0\).  Since \(B\mathbf1=0\),
\[
BK^j\mathbf1=K^jB\mathbf1=0,
\qquad j=0,\ldots,n-1.
\]
The reachability matrix
\([\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1]\) has rank \(n\), so these
equalities imply \(B=0\).  Hence the differential is injective on all of
\(\mathfrak g_n\), not merely in one selected direction.

The constant-rank theorem now makes the image of \(\psi_K\) near the identity
a smooth immersed manifold of dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For every
\(M\in\mathcal G_n\),
\[
\beta\psi_K(M)^j\mathbf1=\beta K^j\mathbf1\qquad(j\ge0),
\]
so the recalled orbit-fibre result places this entire manifold in the visible
fibre.  Finally, all entries of \(M^{-1}KM\) and all components of
\((I-M^{-1}KM)\mathbf1\) depend continuously on \(M\).  Their values at
\(M=I\) are strictly positive; a sufficiently small identity neighbourhood
therefore remains inside the interior Markovian cone.  The stabilizer has zero
Lie algebra by injectivity of the differential, and quotienting by the finite
reset-preserving permutation group cannot change local dimension.  This proves
all assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Nonminimal and graph-specific open interfaces]
\label{rem:nstate-identifiability-open-interfaces-main}
The characterization and the two headline results deliberately assume
Hankel/minimal rank \(n\). If a nominal
\(n\)-state representation has lower visible rank, equal laws need not be
related by an invertible \(n\times n\) similarity; a sharp classification then
requires a stratified treatment of nonminimal augmentations. For a fixed
nonserial zero pattern on the boundary of the Markovian cone, evaluating the
orbit intersection \(\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)\) is an exact semialgebraic
problem, but no graph-uniform closed form is claimed here. Finally, collision
multiplicity is population-identifiable in the serial model but statistically
singular under noisy finite records. These are explicit interfaces, not
consequences of the present results.
\end{remark}

For orientation, the unrestricted fibre is already nontrivial in two states:
\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\1/2&1/4\end{pmatrix},\qquad
M=\begin{pmatrix}9/10&1/10\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
M^{-1}KM=\begin{pmatrix}9/20&1/45\\9/20&3/10\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both kernels are nonnegative and substochastic,
\(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(e_2^\top M=e_2^\top\), and their entire visible
renewal laws coincide, although the hidden kernels do not.

\begin{paperthm}[Quotient inverse]\label{thm:toeplitz_image_inverse_duality}
Work in the same constrained D-MAP record model.  Let
\[
r_0=\rho,\qquad r_1=\rho a,\qquad r_2=\rho u_2,
\]
and assume the quotient inverse domain
\[
r_0>0,\qquad \Delta_{\rm inv}:=r_1-r_0^2\ne0 .
\]
Define
\[
a(r)=\frac{r_1}{r_0},\qquad
\lambda(r)=\frac{r_2-r_0^2}{r_1-r_0^2},
\]
and
\[
\Phi(r)=
\left(1-a(r)+\lambda(r),\,
r_0(1-\lambda(r))-a(r)+\lambda(r)\right).
\]
On the constrained D-MAP image,
\[
\Phi(r)=(p+s,ps).
\]
Thus the visible law determines the unordered survival-factor pair
\(\{p,s\}\), equivalently the unordered roots of
\[
z^2-\Phi_1(r)z+\Phi_2(r)=0,
\]
and determines all visible renewal probabilities through this quotient.  For
known design interval \(\Delta\tau\), the same quotient determines the
unordered numerical rate set
\[
\left\{-\frac{\log p}{\Delta\tau},-\frac{\log s}{\Delta\tau}\right\}
=\{\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\}.
\]
If \(\Delta\tau\) is not supplied as a known design interval, the numerical
rate display is replaced by the dimensionless identifiable set
\[
\{-\log p,-\log s\}
=\{\Gamma\Delta\tau,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\}.
\]
In either case the visible law does not determine an ordered labelled vector
\((\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r})\) unless external side information fixes the
physical assignment.  On the exchange diagonal, the
invariant visible-law estimand is the common dimensionless product, and only
for known \(\Delta\tau\) the common numerical rate, not an ordered
attempt/recovery label.
\end{paperthm}

\begin{paperthm}[Single-record complete visible-law specification test]
\label{thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main}
Fix $0<\varepsilon<M<\infty$, put

\[
\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}=[\varepsilon,M]^2,
\qquad \mathcal P_0=\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\},
\]

where $P_\theta$ is the stationary visible law of the sampled-counter kernels
at the dimensionless parameter $\theta=(x,y)$.  For a binary word
$w=(w_1,\ldots,w_m)$, write

\[
P_\theta[w]=\pi_\theta T_{w_1}(\theta)\cdots
T_{w_m}(\theta)\mathbf1,
\]

where $\pi_\theta$ is stationary for $T_0(\theta)+T_1(\theta)$.  On
stationary binary laws define

\[
d(P,Q)=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}4^{-m}
\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^m}|P[w]-Q[w]|,
\qquad
d(P,\mathcal P_0)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}d(P,P_\theta).
\]

For a record $A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1}$ with $N\ge3$, let

\[
\widehat P_N[w]=\frac1{N-m+1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-m}
\mathbf1_{\{A_j\cdots A_{j+m-1}=w\}},
\qquad
L_N=\max\left\{3,\left\lfloor\frac18\log_2N\right\rfloor\right\},
\]

and set

\[
d_N=\min_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\sum_{m=1}^{L_N}4^{-m}\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^m}
|\widehat P_N[w]-P_\theta[w]|.
\]

Choose a minimizer $\widehat\theta_N$ by a fixed lexicographic rule.  Delete
the initial and terminal incomplete cycles and denote the remaining complete
zero gaps by $G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}$.  If $g_\theta$ is the model Palm gap
mass function, define

\[
h_\theta(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=1\}}
-\frac{g_\theta(1)}{g_\theta(2)}\mathbf1_{\{k=2\}}.
\]

When $K_N\ge3$, put

\[
\widehat\nu_N=\frac1{K_N}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_j)^2,
\qquad
\widehat I_N=\frac{K_N}{N}\widehat\nu_N^2,
\]

\[
Z_N=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\widehat I_N}}
\sum_{j=1}^{K_N-1}
h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_j)h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_{j+1}).
\]

If $K_N<3$ or $\widehat I_N=0$, set $Z_N=0$.  Thus, for every binary
record of length $N\ge3$, the test

\[
\varphi_N=\mathbf1_{\{d_N>N^{-1/4}\ \text{or}\ Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}
\tag{F}
\]

is defined without empirical roots, logarithms, or evaluations of the analytic
root chart outside its domain.  It has the following properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Its null size is compact-uniform:
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\left|\PP_\theta(\varphi_N=1)-\alpha\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This includes the exchange diagonal and every null triangular array, in
particular arrays satisfying $N^{1/4}|p_N-s_N|=O(1)$.

\item If $P$ is a fixed stationary ergodic binary law and
$d(P,\mathcal P_0)>0$, then
\[
\PP_P(\varphi_N=1)\longrightarrow1.
\]
The convergence is uniform on any class with a common geometric
$\alpha$-mixing envelope $\alpha_P(k)\le Cq^k$, $q<1$, and a common
separation $d(P,\mathcal P_0)\ge\delta>0$.  No consistency assertion is made
for arbitrary stationary nonergodic mixtures.

\item Fix an interior exchange point $\theta_0=(x_0,x_0)$, and abbreviate
$g_k=g_{\theta_0}(k)$, $\mu=\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)g_k$, and
\[
h(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=1\}}-\frac{g_1}{g_2}\mathbf1_{\{k=2\}}.
\]
For $0\le\eta<g_2/g_1$, the transition matrix
\[
Q_\eta(\ell\mid k)=g_\ell\{1+\eta h(k)h(\ell)\}
\tag{G}
\]
is stochastic, has stationary marginal $g$, and defines by Palm inversion a
stationary nonrenewal visible law when $\eta>0$.  This law preserves exactly
the sampled-counter coordinates $r_0,r_1,r_2$, because
\[
r_0=\mu^{-1},\qquad r_1=\mu^{-1}g_0,
\qquad r_2=\mu^{-1}\{g_1+g_0Q_\eta(0\mid0)\},
\]
and $Q_\eta(0\mid0)=g_0$.  Nevertheless,
\[
\PP_\eta(10101)=\mu^{-1}g_1^2(1+\eta),
\]
so a length-five word separates every $\eta>0$ from the renewal null.

\item Put
\[
\nu=\EE_g h(G)^2=g_1+\frac{g_1^2}{g_2},
\qquad \mathcal I=\frac{\nu^2}{\mu}.
\]
Along $\eta_N=t/\sqrt N$, $t\ge0$, the stationary record experiments in
part~\textup{(iii)} satisfy
\[
\log\frac{dP_{\eta_N}^{(N)}}{dP_0^{(N)}}
=t\Delta_N-\frac12t^2\mathcal I+o_{P_0}(1),
\qquad \Delta_N\Rightarrow N(0,\mathcal I).
\]
Moreover, $\widehat I_N\to_P\mathcal I$ and
\[
Z_N\Rightarrow N(t\sqrt{\mathcal I},1),
\qquad
\pi_\alpha(t)=1-\Phi_{\rm N}
\{z_{1-\alpha}-t\sqrt{\mathcal I}\}.
\]
Thus $\pi_\alpha(t)>\alpha$ for every $t>0$.  If
$\eta_N=o(N^{-1/2})$, the Kullback--Leibler divergence tends to zero, while
the score component of \textup{(F)} attains the Neyman--Pearson power envelope
of this one-dimensional Gaussian-shift subexperiment at the $N^{-1/2}$
rate.
\end{enumerate}

The distributional-distance guard in parts~\textup{(i)}--\textup{(ii)} is a
specialization of established stationary-ergodic testing methods
\cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,Ryabko2012StationaryTesting}.  Generic
LAN and Gaussian-shift optimality are also standard
\cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.  The model-specific assertions are
the exchange-uniform finite-range score, the exactly
$(r_0,r_1,r_2)$-preserving alternative \textup{(G)}, and their joint use with
the complete visible-law guard.
\end{paperthm}

\begin{proposition}[Sharp local-null Helmert coupling boundary]
\label{prop:helmert-growing-layer-sharp-main}
Retain the exchange-point notation of
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}, put
$p_0=e^{-x_0}$, and write
\[
 S_j=\PP_g(G\geq j)=p_0^j(1+x_0j),\qquad j\geq0.
\]
For $j\geq0$ define the weighted Helmert contrast
\[
 e_j(k)=
 \sqrt{\frac{S_{j+1}}{g_jS_j}}\,\mathbf1_{\{k=j\}}
 -\sqrt{\frac{g_j}{S_jS_{j+1}}}\,\mathbf1_{\{k\geq j+1\}}.
 \tag{V}
\]
Thus $e_0$ is the contrast used in
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}, and
$e_0,e_1,\ldots$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(g)$.  For $J\geq1$ let
\[
 \boldsymbol\Phi_J=
 \bigl(e_a\otimes e_b:0\leq a,b\leq J,\ (a,b)\neq(0,0)\bigr),
 \qquad d_J=(J+1)^2-1,
 \tag{W}
\]
in any fixed order, and let $\mathbf Z_{J,N}$ be the corresponding vector of
scores in \textup{(Q)}, with the basis in \textup{(V)} fixed at $\theta_0$.
Set $n_N=N/\mu$, fix $C<\infty$, and let $\mathcal H_N(C)$ be the physical
sampled-counter null parameters $\sigma$ satisfying
$\|\sqrt N(\sigma-\sigma_0)\|\leq C$, as in \textup{(T)}.  If
$J_N\to\infty$, the following condition is necessary and sufficient:
\[
 n_NS_{J_N}^2\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{X}
\]
More precisely, \textup{(X)} is equivalent to the existence, on extensions of
the probability spaces, of
$\boldsymbol\xi_{N,\sigma}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{d_{J_N}})$ such that, for every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \sup_{\sigma\in\mathcal H_N(C)}
 \PP_\sigma\!\left(
  \|\mathbf Z_{J_N,N}-\boldsymbol\xi_{N,\sigma}\|_2>\varepsilon
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{Y}
\]
In particular, the same equivalence holds at the fixed exchange point
$\sigma_0$.

Replacing the deterministic cycle count by the
calendar stopping index and replacing $\mu$ by $\widehat\mu_N$ contribute,
respectively,
\[
 O_P(J_NN^{-1/4})\quad\hbox{and}\quad O_P(J_NN^{-1/2})
 \tag{Z}
\]
in Euclidean norm.  The local null covariance perturbation contributes
$O_P(J_N^3N^{-1/2})$; all three terms are uniformly $o_P(1)$ under
\textup{(X)}.

The necessity in \textup{(X)} already follows from the fact that a standard
Gaussian limit for the moving corner coordinate
$e_{J_N}\otimes e_{J_N}$ requires
\[
 n_NS_{J_N}^2\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{AA}
\]
More strongly, if some $r_N<J_N$ satisfies
$n_NS_{r_N}^2\to0$ and $J_N-r_N\asymp J_N$, then, with probability tending
to one, every score in the block
\[
 \{e_a\otimes e_b:r_N\leq a,b\leq J_N\}
 \tag{AB}
\]
is zero.  The corresponding standard Gaussian block has
$(J_N-r_N+1)^2$ degrees of freedom, so neither an unweighted chi-square
approximation for that block nor an $o_P(1)$ Euclidean coupling can hold.

In the second-order band
$2x_0J_N=\log n_N+O(\log\log n_N)$, put
\[
 \omega_N=\log n_N+2\log\log n_N-2x_0J_N.
\]
Then \textup{(Y)} holds if and only if $\omega_N\to\infty$.  Equivalently,
the sharp second-order region is
\[
 J_N\leq
 \frac{\log n_N+2\log\log n_N-\omega_N}{2x_0}
 \tag{AC}
\]
for some $\omega_N\to\infty$.
If
$2x_0J_N=\log n_N+2\log\log n_N-c+o(1)$ for a fixed $c\in\mathbb R$, then
$n_NS_{J_N}^2\to e^c/4$, so \textup{(Y)} fails.  The previously verified
necessary boundary is therefore also sufficient; no assertion of Le Cam
equivalence is made.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The equal-rate dictionary gives the displayed formula for $S_j$.
The two values in \textup{(V)} have weighted mean zero and weighted squared
norm one.  Nested supports then give
$\langle e_j,e_k\rangle_{L^2(g)}=0$ for $j\neq k$; completeness follows by
successively separating the atoms $0,1,\ldots$ from the remaining tail.
Since $S_{j+1}/S_j\to p_0$ and $g_j/S_j\to1-p_0$,
\[
 \|e_j\|_\infty\asymp S_j^{-1/2},\qquad
 \max_{a,b\leq J}\|e_a\otimes e_b\|_\infty\asymp S_J^{-1}.
 \tag{1}
\]

For the deterministic-cycle argument, let
$K_J(k)=\sum_{a=0}^Je_a(k)^2$.  Adding the constant function to the Helmert
contrasts gives the projection onto the partition
$\{0\},\ldots,\{J\},\{J+1,J+2,\ldots\}$; hence
\[
 1+K_J(k)=
 \begin{cases}
  g_k^{-1},&0\leq k\leq J,\\
  S_{J+1}^{-1},&k\geq J+1.

\begin{theorem}[Complete Markov--Palm tangent space and pointwise omnibus score]
\label{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}
Fix $0<\alpha<1$, an interior exchange point $\theta_0=(x_0,x_0)$, and let
$g=(g_k)_{k\geq0}$ be its Palm zero-gap law.  Thus $g_k>0$,
$\mu=\sum_{k\geq0}(k+1)g_k<\infty$, and, for this sampled-counter law,
$g$ has an exponential tail.  Put
\[
 \mathsf H=L^2(g\otimes g),\qquad
 \mathsf H_{\rm int}=\{q\in\mathsf H:
 \EE(q\mid G_0)=\EE(q\mid G_1)=0\},
\]
where $G_0,G_1$ are independent with law $g$, and define
\[
 \mathsf T=\{q\in\mathsf H_{\rm int}:q(0,0)=0\}.
 \tag{H}
\]
Consider all quadratic-mean differentiable Markov-gap paths
\[
 Q_t(\ell\mid k)=g_\ell w_t(k,\ell),\qquad w_0=1,
 \qquad \left\|\frac{2(\sqrt{w_t}-1)}t-q\right\|_{\mathsf H}
 \longrightarrow0,
\tag{I}
\]
whose rows sum to one, for which $gQ_t=g$, and which preserve
$(r_0,r_1,r_2)$ to first order.  Then the following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The closed tangent space of these paths is exactly $\mathsf T$; in
particular it is infinite dimensional.  If
\[
 u_0(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=0\}}-g_0,\qquad
 v_0(k,\ell)=u_0(k)u_0(\ell),
\]
then
\[
 \mathsf T=\mathsf H_{\rm int}\ominus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\}.
 \tag{J}
\]
Every $q\in\mathsf T$ is realized by a two-sided path in \textup{(I)} whose
kernels satisfy a Doeblin minorization by $(1-o(1))g$ and preserve $g$ and
all three inclusion coordinates exactly.  A nonzero such path is nonrenewal
for all sufficiently small nonzero $t$.

\item Every adjacent-pair score generated by a quadratic-mean differentiable
renewal marginal path belongs to the closed span of
$s(G_0)+s(G_1)$, with $s\in L^2_0(g)$.  Hence the sampled-counter renewal
nuisance space is orthogonal to $\mathsf T$.  On the ambient space
$\mathsf H$, the efficient information operator for the Markov interaction
is
\[
 \mathcal I_{\rm eff}=\mu^{-1}\Pi_{\mathsf T},
 \tag{K}
\]
where
\[
 \Pi_{\mathsf T}f=f-\EE(f\mid G_0)-\EE(f\mid G_1)+\EE f
 -\frac{\langle f,v_0\rangle_{\mathsf H}}
 {\|v_0\|_{\mathsf H}^2}v_0.
 \tag{L}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \ker\mathcal I_{\rm eff}
 =\mathsf H_{\rm int}^{\perp}\oplus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\},
 \qquad
 \left.\mathcal I_{\rm eff}\right|_{\mathsf T}
 =\mu^{-1}I_{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{M}
\]

\item Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles from a stationary record and
write its complete gaps as $G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}$, where
$K_N/N\to_P\mu^{-1}$.  For $q\in\mathsf T$, let
\[

\]
For each fixed finite collection $q_1,\ldots,q_d\in\mathsf T$, the null

\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\operatorname{Cov}
 \{\Delta_N(q_a),\Delta_N(q_b)\}
 =\mu^{-1}\langle q_a,q_b\rangle_{\mathsf H}.
 \tag{N}
\]

\[

\textup{(N)}, rather than a $\mathsf T$-valued normal random element with
identity covariance.  No uniform-LAN assertion over arbitrary norm-compact
subsets of $\mathsf T$ is made.

\begin{paperthm}[Fixed-setting retained-record inclusion CLT]\label{thm:finite-record-inference-audit-main}
Assume the stationary model in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main} and
retain only cycles fully observed within the length-\(N\) record.  Form the
complete-cycle inclusion estimator
\[
\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc}
=\left(\frac1N\sum_{j\in J_{0,N}}U_j^{(0)},
       \frac1N\sum_{j\in J_{1,N}}U_j^{(1)},
       \frac1N\sum_{j\in J_{2,N}}U_j^{(2)}\right)^\top ,
\qquad
\Rinc=(r_0,r_1,r_2)^\top .
\]
In Palm cycle coordinates put
\[
U_j=
\bigl(1,\mathbf1_{\{G_j=0\}},
\mathbf1_{\{G_j=1\}}+\mathbf1_{\{G_j=0,G_{j+1}=0\}}\bigr)^\top,
\qquad
L_j=G_j+1,\qquad
Y_j=U_j-\Rinc L_j .
\]

\[

\Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,\Sigma_r),
\]
where
\[
\Sigma_r=\frac1\mu\{\operatorname{Var}(Y_0)
+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_1)+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,Y_0)\},
\qquad \mu=\EE L_0 .
\]
The separated-batch covariance estimator with
\(b_N=\lfloor N^{1/3}\rfloor\), plug-in centering, and the operational gate
\(M_N\ge m_N\), where \(m_N\to\infty\) and \(m_N=o(N/b_N)\), obeys
\[

\]
on an event whose probability tends to one.
\end{paperthm}

\begin{proposition}[Exact three-inclusion image]
\label{prop:exact-three-inclusion-image-main}
Let \(r=(r_0,r_1,r_2)\) be a real triple in the stable inverse chart
\(r_0>0\), \(r_1-r_0^2\ne0\), form
\(\sigma=\Phi(r)=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\), and suppose the roots \(p,s\) of
\(z^2-\sigma_1z+\sigma_2\) belong to \((0,1)\), with equality allowed.  Define
\[
\mathfrak C(p,s)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{s\log p-p\log s}{\log p-\log s},&p\ne s,\\[6pt]
p(1-\log p),&p=s,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\mathcal E(r)=\frac{r_1}{r_0}-1+\mathfrak C(p,s).
\]
Then \(r\) is generated by positive sampled-counter parameters
\((\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)\) if and only if
\(\mathcal E(r)=0\).  On the distinct-root stratum this is a regular
codimension-one real-analytic hypersurface.  The symmetric function
\(\mathfrak C\) has a real-analytic continuation in \((\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\)
through \(p=s\); the physical image at the exchange diagonal is the feasible
side of the continued hypersurface and hence has a boundary there.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For necessity, put \(x=\Gamma\Delta\tau\), \(y=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\),
so \(p=e^{-x}\), \(s=e^{-y}\), and
\[
b=\frac{y(p-s)}{y-x}.
\]
The continuous diagonal interpretation is understood.  Direct cancellation
gives
\[
s+b=\frac{yp-xs}{y-x}
=\frac{s\log p-p\log s}{\log p-\log s}=\mathfrak C(p,s).
\]
Since \(a=1-s-b\), this proves \(\mathcal E(r)=0\).

Conversely, choose any \(\Delta\tau>0\), set
\(\Gamma=-\log p/\Delta\tau\),
\(\kappa_{\mathrm r}=-\log s/\Delta\tau\), and define
\(b=\mathfrak C(p,s)-s\), \(a=1-\mathfrak C(p,s)\).  These are precisely the
strictly positive integral weights in the sampled-counter kernels.  The first
symmetric-coordinate identity gives
\(\lambda=p+s+a-1=p-b\), while the second gives
\[
r_0=\frac{ps+a-\lambda}{1-\lambda}
=\frac{(1-p)(1-s)}{1-p+b}=\rho.
\]
The definitions of \(a(r)\) and \(\lambda(r)\) then recover \(r_1=\rho a\)
and \(r_2=\rho^2+\lambda(r_1-\rho^2)\), proving sufficiency.

For regularity, write
\[
D(\sigma)=1-\sigma_1+\sigma_2=(1-p)(1-s),\qquad
Q(\sigma)=1-\sigma_1+\mathfrak C(p,s).
\]
On the inverse chart, the change of variables
\(r\mapsto(r_0,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\) is locally invertible: in the intermediate
coordinates \((r_0,a,\lambda)\), the determinant of
\(\partial(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)/\partial(a,\lambda)\) is \(r_0>0\).  Moreover,
\[
\mathcal E(r)=Q(\sigma)-\frac{D(\sigma)}{r_0}
=\frac{Q(\sigma)}{r_0}
\left\{r_0-\frac{D(\sigma)}{Q(\sigma)}\right\}.
\]
Thus its zero set is the graph \(r_0=D/Q\), so it is regular.  Away from the
diagonal analyticity is immediate.  At \(p=m+d\), \(s=m-d\), both the
numerator and denominator defining \(\mathfrak C\) are analytic odd functions
of \(d\) for \(|d|<m\), and the denominator has a simple zero at \(d=0\).
Their quotient therefore has a removable analytic extension; invariance under
\(d\mapsto-d\) makes that extension even.  Its Taylor expansion begins
\[
\mathfrak C(m+d,m-d)=m(1-\log m)
+\frac{d^2}{m}\left(\frac12+\frac13\log m\right)+O(d^4).
\]
Since \(m=\sigma_1/2\) and \(d^2=\sigma_1^2/4-\sigma_2\), this supplies the
claimed symmetric analytic continuation.  The real-root constraint is the
one-sided inequality \(\sigma_2\le\sigma_1^2/4\), which proves the final
boundary qualification.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Analytic joint image chart at the exchange boundary]
\label{prop:analytic-joint-image-chart-main}
Fix \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\) and let

\[
\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}
=\{(x,y):\varepsilon\le x,y\le M\}.
\]
For \(\sigma_1>0\), \(\sigma_2>0\), put
\[
w(\sigma)=1-\frac{4\sigma_2}{\sigma_1^2}
\]
and, for \(w<1\), define
\[
H(w)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\sqrt w}{\operatorname{artanh}\sqrt w},&0<w<1,\\[5pt]
1,&w=0,\\[2pt]
\dfrac{\sqrt{-w}}{\arctan\sqrt{-w}},&w<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(H\) is real analytic on \((-\infty,1)\), with
\[
H(w)=1-\frac w3-\frac{4w^2}{45}+O(w^3)
\quad(w\longrightarrow0).
\]
The symmetric continuation in
\Cref{prop:exact-three-inclusion-image-main} has the root-free expression
\[
\mathfrak C_{\rm an}(\sigma)
=\frac{\sigma_1}{2}
\left\{1-\frac12\log(\sigma_2)
H\!\left(1-\frac{4\sigma_2}{\sigma_1^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Consequently there is an open neighbourhood \(\mathcal U\) of the compact
three-inclusion image of \(\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\) on which
\[
e(r)=\frac{r_1}{r_0}-1+\mathfrak C_{\rm an}\{\Phi(r)\},
\qquad
\mathcal D(r)=\Phi_1(r)^2-4\Phi_2(r)
\]
are real analytic and
\[
r\text{ is a positive sampled-counter image point}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
e(r)=0,\qquad \mathcal D(r)\ge0.
\]
Moreover, with \(\psi=(e,\mathcal D)^\top\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}D\psi(r)=2
\]
at every physical point in this compact image, including the exchange
diagonal.  The equivalence is local to \(\mathcal U\); no global extension
of the logarithmic chart is asserted.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(m=\sigma_1/2\).  On the real-root side set
\[
p=m(1+t),\qquad s=m(1-t),\qquad t^2=w.
\]
Direct expansion of the numerator gives
\[
s\log p-p\log s
=m\{2\operatorname{artanh}t-t\log(\sigma_2)\}.
\]
Division by
\(\log p-\log s=2\operatorname{artanh}t\) proves the displayed formula.
The power series of \(t/\operatorname{artanh}t\) contains only even powers
and begins with the stated coefficients.  Replacing \(t\) by
\(i\sqrt{-w}\) gives the real expression on \(w<0\), so the two formulas
are restrictions of one real-analytic germ through \(w=0\).

On the compact physical image,
\(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\) are bounded away from zero and \(w\) is bounded away
from one.  The quotient denominator is also uniformly separated from zero
by \Cref{prop:stable-quotient-chart-main}.  A sufficiently small uniform
neighbourhood therefore lies in the displayed analytic chart and has both
quadratic roots in \((0,1)\) whenever \(\mathcal D\ge0\).  The image
equivalence now follows from
\Cref{prop:exact-three-inclusion-image-main}.

For the rank assertion use the analytic coordinates
\((r_0,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\).  With
\[
D(\sigma)=1-\sigma_1+\sigma_2,
\qquad
Q(\sigma)=1-\sigma_1+\mathfrak C_{\rm an}(\sigma),
\]
the calculation in the proof of
\Cref{prop:exact-three-inclusion-image-main} gives
\[
e(r)=Q(\sigma)-\frac{D(\sigma)}{r_0},
\qquad
\frac{\partial e}{\partial r_0}
=\frac{D(\sigma)}{r_0^2}>0.
\]
By contrast,
\[
\frac{\partial\mathcal D}{\partial r_0}=0,
\qquad
\nabla_\sigma\mathcal D=(2\sigma_1,-4)\ne0.
\]
Thus the two rows of \(D\psi\) are linearly independent.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform joint three-inclusion physical-image test]
\label{thm:uniform-joint-physical-image-test-main}
Fix \(0<\varepsilon<M<\infty\), and let \(\mathcal U\), \(e\),
\(\mathcal D\), and \(\psi=(e,\mathcal D)^\top\) be as in
\Cref{prop:analytic-joint-image-chart-main}.  Choose, before observing the
record, a closed neighbourhood \(\mathcal U_0\) of the compact physical
image such that \(\mathcal U_0\subset\mathcal U\), and put
\[
\widehat r_N=\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc},
\qquad
\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat r_N\in\mathcal U_0\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal G_N\), define
\[
J(r)=D\psi(r),qquad
\widehat\Omega_N
=J(\widehat r_N)\widehat\Sigma_{r,N}^{\rm tot}
J(\widehat r_N)^\top .
\]
Let \(\widehat\Omega_N^{\rm tr}\) be obtained by replacing every eigenvalue
of \(\widehat\Omega_N\) below \(N^{-1/4}\) by \(N^{-1/4}\), and write
\[
\widehat\Omega_N^{\rm tr}
=\begin{pmatrix}
\widehat\omega_{11,N}&\widehat\omega_{12,N}\\
\widehat\omega_{12,N}&\widehat\omega_{22,N}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set
\[
\widehat\beta_N
=\frac{\widehat\omega_{12,N}}{\widehat\omega_{11,N}},
\qquad
\widehat v_N
=\widehat\omega_{22,N}
-\frac{\widehat\omega_{12,N}^2}{\widehat\omega_{11,N}},
\]
\[
Z_{e,N}
=\frac{\sqrt N\,e(\widehat r_N)}
{\sqrt{\widehat\omega_{11,N}}},
\qquad
Z_{d,N}
=\frac{\sqrt N\{\mathcal D(\widehat r_N)
-\widehat\beta_Ne(\widehat r_N)\}}
{\sqrt{\widehat v_N}},
\]
and
\[
T_N=Z_{e,N}^2+(Z_{d,N}^{-})^2,
\qquad z^-:=\max\{-z,0\}.
\]
For \(0<\alpha<1\), let
\[
c_{1,\alpha}=F_{\chi_1^2}^{-1}(1-\alpha)
\]
and let \(c_{\partial,\alpha}\) be the unique solution of
\[
\frac12F_{\chi_1^2}(c_{\partial,\alpha})
+\frac12F_{\chi_2^2}(c_{\partial,\alpha})=1-\alpha.
\]
With \(\kappa_N=\log N\), use
\[
c_{N,\alpha}=
\begin{cases}
c_{1,\alpha},&Z_{d,N}>\kappa_N,\\
c_{\partial,\alpha},&Z_{d,N}\le\kappa_N.
\end{cases}
\]
The operational procedure rejects when
\(\mathcal G_N\cap\{T_N>c_{N,\alpha}\}\) occurs and otherwise withholds
the report off \(\mathcal G_N\).  For a total-space mathematical test, the
off-gate decision is defined to be no rejection.

Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Uniformly on \(\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\),
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{r,N}^{\rm tot}-\Sigma_r(\theta)
\longrightarrow_{\PP_\theta}0,
\qquad
\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\lambda_{\min}\{J(r(\theta))\Sigma_r(\theta)J(r(\theta))^\top\}>0.
\]
The convergence is uniform in probability, and the chart gate and spectral
truncation are inactive with probability tending to one uniformly in
\(\theta\).

\item At every fixed physical point with \(p\ne s\),
\[
T_N\Rightarrow\chi_1^2,
\qquad
\PP_\theta\{Z_{d,N}>\kappa_N\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
At every fixed exchange-diagonal point,
\[
T_N\Rightarrow Z_1^2+(Z_2^-)^2
\sim\frac12\chi_1^2+\frac12\chi_2^2,
\]
where \(Z_1,Z_2\) are independent standard normal variables.  In particular,
\[
c_{1,0.05}=3.8414588\ldots,\qquad
c_{\partial,0.05}=5.1383808\ldots .
\]

\item The test has compact-uniform asymptotic size at most \(\alpha\):
\[
\limsup_{N\to\infty}
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\PP_\theta\{\mathcal G_N,\ T_N>c_{N,\alpha}\}
\le\alpha.
\]
More precisely, along a null sequence define
\[
\eta_N=
\frac{\sqrt N\,(p_N-s_N)^2}
{\sqrt{v(\theta_N)}},
\qquad
v=\omega_{22}-\frac{\omega_{12}^2}{\omega_{11}}.
\]
If \(\eta_N\to\eta<\infty\), then
\[
T_N\Rightarrow Z_1^2+(Z_2+\eta)^-{}^2
\]
and the boundary critical value is selected with probability tending to one.
If \(\eta_N\to\infty\), then
\(T_N-Z_{e,N}^2\to_{\PP}0\); if also
\(\eta_N/\log N\to\infty\), the interior critical value is selected with
probability tending to one.

\item Let a stationary full-support renewal alternative have an exponential
gap moment, a limiting inclusion triple \(r\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal U_0\),
and the complete-cycle CLT and covariance consistency in Theorem~C with a
positive-definite constraint covariance.  If \(e(r)\ne0\) or
\(\mathcal D(r)<0\), then \(T_N\to_{\PP}\infty\).  Thus the stated
consistency conclusion is conditional on an explicit renewal alternative;
no test of arbitrary nonrenewal time-series misspecification is claimed.
\end{enumerate}
The chi-bar-square and boundary-selection principles are standard
\cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio,Shapiro1987MetricProjection,
Andrews2001BoundaryTesting}; the theorem is their studentized specialization
to the sampled-counter three-inclusion image, including the uniform
nondegeneracy verification below.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On \(\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\), both eigenvalues of the zero-labelled kernel
are at most \(e^{-\varepsilon}\).  At a repeated eigenvalue its powers carry
only a first-degree Jordan factor.  Hence, for constants independent of
\(\theta\),
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\PP_\theta(G\ge k)\le C(1+k)e^{-\varepsilon k},
\qquad k\ge0.
\]
Every exponential moment of \(G\) of order below \(\varepsilon\) is
therefore uniformly bounded.  The complete-cycle reward in Theorem~C is a
function of two consecutive independent gaps, so the corresponding
triangular arrays are \(1\)-dependent and have uniformly bounded fourth
moments.  The usual even--odd blocking proof of the \(1\)-dependent CLT is
then uniform along every convergent parameter sequence.  The renewal-count
replacement and the two endpoint deletions are uniform by the same
exponential bound.  Compactness and the subsequence criterion give the
uniform bounded-Lipschitz CLT.  The maximal and Chernoff bounds in the proof
of \Cref{lem:paper-level-separated-covariance-main} use only these uniform
moment constants, so they also give the stated uniform covariance
consistency.

It remains to prove nondegeneracy rather than assume it.  If
\(c^\top\Sigma_rc=0\), put
\[
f(i,j)=c^\top
\left[
\begin{pmatrix}
1\\ \mathbf1_{\{i=0\}}\\
\mathbf1_{\{i=1\}}+\mathbf1_{\{i=0,j=0\}}
\end{pmatrix}
-r(i+1)
\right].
\]
For a full-support i.i.d. gap law, the Hoeffding row--column decomposition
of a one-dependent sequence says that its long-run variance is zero exactly
when \(f(i,j)=u_i-u_j\).  The degenerate interaction residual of \(f\) is
\[
c_2(\mathbf1_{\{i=0\}}-g_0)
(\mathbf1_{\{j=0\}}-g_0).
\]
Since \(0<g_0<1\), vanishing of the interaction forces \(c_2=0\).  Then
\(f\) depends only on \(i\), and an identity \(f(i)=u_i-u_j\) for all
\(i,j\) forces \(f\equiv0\).  For all \(i\ge1\), this reads
\[
c_0-(c^\top r)(i+1)=0,
\]
so \(c^\top r=c_0=0\); the value \(i=0\) then gives \(c_1=0\).  Thus
\(c=0\), and \(\Sigma_r\) is positive definite.  Its entries are continuous
in \(\theta\) by dominated convergence.  Compactness and the rank-two
conclusion of \Cref{prop:analytic-joint-image-chart-main} now give the
uniform positive lower bound for \(\Omega=J\Sigma_rJ^\top\).

For any positive-definite
\(\Omega=(\omega_{ij})_{i,j=1}^2\), direct completion of squares gives
\[
\inf_{u\ge0}
\left\|\binom e{d-u}\right\|_{\Omega^{-1}}^2
=\frac{e^2}{\omega_{11}}
+\frac{\{d-(\omega_{12}/\omega_{11})e\}_{-}^2}
{\omega_{22}-\omega_{12}^2/\omega_{11}}.
\]
Hence \(T_N\) is exactly the estimated covariance-metric distance to
\(\{0\}\times[0,\infty)\).  Residualization makes its two Gaussian limits
independent.  At a fixed interior point the standardized slack diverges to
\(+\infty\), leaving one squared normal.  At the boundary it is centered,
and conditioning on its sign gives the equal mixture of one and two degrees
of freedom.

For uniform size, take an arbitrary null sequence and a convergent parameter
subsequence.  If \(\eta_N\) is bounded, take a further subsequence on which
it converges.  The sequential CLT gives the asserted limit, and
\((z+\eta)^-\le z^-\) for \(\eta\ge0\) shows stochastic domination by the
boundary law.  If \(\eta_N\to\infty\), its negative part vanishes in
probability and \(c_{N,\alpha}\ge c_{1,\alpha}\), so the rejection
probability has upper limit at most \(\alpha\).  The usual
near-maximizing-sequence contradiction proves the displayed supremum bound.
Finally, under the explicit alternative assumptions, the continuous mapping
theorem makes \(N^{-1}T_N\) converge to the strictly positive squared
distance from \(\psi(r)\) to the constraint cone, proving consistency.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Dominated renewal local power]
\label{prop:joint-physical-image-local-power-main}
Fix an exchange-diagonal physical point \(r_\circ\) in
\(\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\), and let \(g^\circ=(g_k^\circ)_{k\ge0}\) be its
Palm gap law, with mean cycle length \(\mu^\circ\).  For
\(\eta=(\eta_\mu,\eta_0,\eta_1)\), define
\[
g_\eta(k)=g^\circ(k)+v_\eta(k),
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
v_\eta(0)&=\eta_0,\\
v_\eta(1)&=\eta_1,\\
v_\eta(2)&=-\eta_\mu-3\eta_0-2\eta_1,\\
v_\eta(3)&=\eta_\mu+2\eta_0+\eta_1,\\
v_\eta(k)&=0,\qquad k\ge4.
\end{aligned}
\]
On a sufficiently small fixed neighbourhood of the origin this is a
full-support probability law.  The resulting stationary renewal experiment
is differentiable in quadratic mean and locally asymptotically normal per
unit calendar time, with information
\[
\mathcal I_{ij}
=\frac1{\mu^\circ}\sum_{k=0}^3
\frac{v_i(k)v_j(k)}{g_k^\circ},
\]
where \(v_i\) denotes the coefficient vector of the \(i\)-th component of
\(\eta\).  The matrix \(\mathcal I\) is positive definite.

All first-order directions in three-inclusion space are represented by this
experiment.  Indeed, for any renewal gap law,
\[
r=\left(\frac1\mu,\frac{g_0}{\mu},
\frac{g_1+g_0^2}{\mu}\right),
\]
and the Jacobian with respect to \((\mu,g_0,g_1)\) is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-\mu^{-2}&0&0\\
-g_0\mu^{-2}&\mu^{-1}&0\\
-(g_1+g_0^2)\mu^{-2}&2g_0\mu^{-1}&\mu^{-1}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det=-\mu^{-4}\ne0.
\]

Let a local sequence in this experiment satisfy
\[
\sqrt N\,e(r_N)\longrightarrow\delta,\qquad
\sqrt N\,\mathcal D(r_N)\longrightarrow\tau.
\]
At \(r_\circ\), write
\[
\Omega=
\begin{pmatrix}\omega_{11}&\omega_{12}\\
\omega_{12}&\omega_{22}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\beta=\frac{\omega_{12}}{\omega_{11}},
\qquad
v=\omega_{22}-\frac{\omega_{12}^2}{\omega_{11}},
\]
and put
\[
a_*=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{\omega_{11}}},
\qquad
b_*=\frac{\tau-\beta\delta}{\sqrt v}.

 succeeded in 414ms:
the expansion on events with probability tending to one.  Slutsky's theorem
and continuity of projection onto the closed half-space give the asserted
limit.  The certificate establishes only that the covariance in this limit is
nonsingular; it is not used to calibrate a procedure.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Proofs of Theorems A--D}\label{subsec:proofs-a-d-main}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~A]
Write \(\beta=e_D^\top\) and
\(c=((1-p),a)^\top\).  The marked kernel has rank-one reset form
\(T_1=c\beta\).  Conditional on every click, the next hidden state is therefore
\(D\), independently of the pre-click state.  Successive click epochs are
regeneration epochs, and the numbers of intervening zeros are independent with
common Palm mass
\[
g_k=\beta T_0^kT_1\mathbf1,\qquad k\ge0.
\]
The entries of \(T_0\) are strictly positive along every admissible serial path,
so \(g_k>0\) for all \(k\); the spectral radius of \(T_0\) is less than one,
and \(\sum_{k\ge0}g_k=1\).  This proves the full-support renewal assertion.

Since \(T_0\) is lower triangular, direct evaluation of \(T_0^k\), followed by
substitution of the integral defining \(b\), gives, off the equal-rate diagonal,
\[
g_k=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-
\Gamma(1-s)s^k}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},\qquad
S_k=\sum_{j\ge k}g_j=
\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k}
{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}.
\]
The continuous limit at \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) follows either by
l'H\^opital's rule or by exponentiating the repeated-eigenvalue triangular
matrix.  Because \(h_k=1-S_{k+1}/S_k\), elementary cancellation yields
\[
h_{k+1}-h_k=
\frac{\Gamma\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)^2p^ks^k}
{(\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k)
 (\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^{k+1}-\Gamma s^{k+1})}>0.
\]
On the diagonal, with \(y=\Gamma\Delta\tau\) and \(p=e^{-y}\), the same
calculation gives
\[
S_k=p^k(1+yk),\qquad
h_{k+1}-h_k=\frac{y^2p}{(1+yk)(1+y(k+1))}>0.
\]

Let \(P=T_0+T_1\) be the hidden transition matrix.  Its eigenvalues are
\(1\) and \(\lambda_{\rm hid}=p-b\).  Conditional on a click at time zero,
the state at time one is \(D\), and hence
\[
u_n:=\PP(A_n=1\mid A_0=1)
=\rho+(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid}^{n-1},\qquad n\ge1.
\]
Multiplication by \(\rho\) gives the covariance formula.  With
\(q=1-p\), stationarity gives
\[
\rho=\frac{q(1-s)}{q+b},\qquad
\rho-a=\frac{b(q-a)}{q+b}>0,
\]
so \(\gamma_1=\rho(a-\rho)<0\) and \(0\)-dependence is excluded.  If
\(\lambda_{\rm hid}=0\), the two rows of \(P\) coincide; the hidden state after
one intervening step has forgotten the past, which makes visible blocks
separated by one omitted observation independent.  Conversely, exact
\(1\)-dependence implies \(\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_2)=0\), and the strict
prefactor in the covariance formula forces \(\lambda_{\rm hid}=0\).
Finally, in a binary renewal process an order-\(m\) Markov property would make
the click hazard constant after every zero run of length at least \(m\).  The
strictly increasing hazards above rule this out for every finite \(m\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~B]
The regenerative reset gives
\[
r_0=\rho,\qquad
r_1=\rho\PP(A_1=1\mid A_0=1)=\rho a,
\qquad r_2=\rho u_2.
\]
The spectral calculation in the proof of Theorem~A gives
\(u_2=\rho+(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid}\).  Therefore, on
\(r_1-r_0^2\ne0\),
\[
a=\frac{r_1}{r_0},qquad
\lambda_{\rm hid}=
\frac{r_2-r_0^2}{r_1-r_0^2}.
\]
Since \(a=1-s-b\) and \(\lambda_{\rm hid}=p-b\),
\[
1-a+\lambda_{\rm hid}=p+s.
\]
Substitution of \(\rho=q(1-s)/(q+b)\), \(q=1-p\), into the second coordinate
gives
\[
\rho(1-\lambda_{\rm hid})-a+\lambda_{\rm hid}=ps.
\]
These are precisely the two coordinates of \(\Phi\).  Their polynomial has
root multiset \(\{p,s\}\).  That multiset determines the displayed Palm gap
law, including its continuous repeated-root limit, and renewal products then
determine every finite inclusion probability; finite inclusion--exclusion
determines every word probability.  Thus the three coordinates are
law-determining.  This argument does not select a physical label for either
root and makes no minimal-cardinality claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~C]
Under Palm sampling, the gaps \((G_j)\) are i.i.d. with an exponential moment.
The displayed cycle reward satisfies \(\EE U_j=\Rinc\EE L_j\), hence
\(\EE Y_j=0\), and it depends only on \((G_j,G_{j+1})\), hence is
\(1\)-dependent.  Complete-cycle deletion removes at most a fixed number of
endpoint cycles; their total length is \(O_{\PP}(\log N)\) by the exponential
moment.  The renewal count satisfies
\(K_N=N/\mu+O_{\PP}(\sqrt N)\).  The random-index version of the
Hoeffding--Robbins CLT for finite-range dependent variables therefore yields
\[
N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=0}^{K_N-1}Y_j
\Rightarrow\mathcal N\!\left(0,
\mu^{-1}\{\Var Y_0+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_1)
+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,Y_0)\}\right).
\]
The endpoint remainder is \(o_{\PP}(1)\) on this scale, proving the stated
linearization and CLT.  Consistency and the rate of the stopped separated-batch
covariance estimator are exactly the content of
\Cref{lem:paper-level-separated-covariance-main}, including plug-in centering
and the strengthened gate \(M_N\ge m_N\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~D]
On the stable quotient chart, \(\Phi\) is continuously differentiable with the
uniform bounds in \Cref{prop:stable-quotient-chart-main}.  Applying the
multivariate delta method to Theorem~C gives the symmetric-coordinate CLT and
its sandwich covariance.  When \(z_-<z_+\), implicit differentiation of
\(z^2-\sigma_1z+\sigma_2=0\) gives the displayed matrix \(J_{\rm root}\).
The sorted roots remain in the same order with probability tending to one, so
a second delta-method application gives the root CLT.  Composition with
\(z\mapsto-\log z/\Delta\tau\) gives \(J_{\rm rate}\) and the root-ordered
rate CLT.  No step assigns the two entries to physical labels.
\end{proof}

The dependencies are linear: Theorem~A supplies the renewal law, Theorem~B the
quotient inverse, Theorem~C the retained-record Gaussian input, Theorem~D the
quotient delta method, and Theorem~E the local projection calculus at the
certified candidate.  Detailed theorem forms, proof lemmas, certificate
interfaces, and implementation algorithms appear below with ordinary section
numbering; they do not add further paper-level theorems.

The sections below record the minimal notation needed for the model, prove the
quantitative higher-state theorem, and compare each result with the canonical
DMAP/DPH/MAP literature.  Detailed regenerative lemmas, implementation
algorithms, diagnostics, and extended comparator tables are supplementary.

\section{D-MAP setting and record-level observables}\label{sec:operational}

We first consider only the stationary D-MAP record law of
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.  The hidden chain has two states, the
output alphabet is \(\{0,1\}\), and the visible output is the stationary
two-sided binary process
\[
(A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z},
\]
where \(A_n=1\) denotes a marked transition of the D-MAP in the \(n\)th
discrete step.  All Palm, covariance, renewal, and independence
statements below refer to this two-sided stationary law.  A finite observed
record of length \(N\) is only the restriction
\[
A^{(N)}=(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_{N-1}),
\]
of the stationary process.  The only nonstationary finite-start convention
used below is the post-burn-in retained-length convention: generate
\(L_N+N\) intervals from an arbitrary hidden initial law, discard the first
\(L_N\), and reindex the retained word as
\((A_{L_N},\ldots,A_{L_N+N-1})\), so \(N\) is always the retained sample size.
Compressing such a finite record to the empirical click
frequency recovers only the one-point observable
\[
\widehat\rho_N=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}A_n.
\]
The full record, however, carries more. In particular, one may ask:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.0em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item what words belong to the support of the stationary law;
\item how the zero-run lengths between clicks are distributed;
\item whether the click hazard after a long run of zeros remembers the run length;
\item how the low-lag covariance sequence behaves;
\item what counting noise remains after coarse time averaging.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{definition}[Record observables]\label{def:record-benchmarks-main}
For a stationary binary record $(A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$, a \emph{zero-run length} is the number $G$ of consecutive zeros following a click and preceding the next click. If the zero-run law has full support, its hazard is
\[
h_k=\PP(G=k\mid G\ge k),\qquad k\ge0 .
\]
A stationary record is \emph{exact $1$-dependent} when, for every $m$, the sigma algebras generated by $\{A_j:j\le m\}$ and $\{A_j:j\ge m+2\}$ are independent.
Equivalently, one leaves the intermediate sample at time $m+1$ unobserved: a block ending at time $m$ is tested for independence from a block beginning at time $m+2$, not conditioned on the middle sample.
\end{definition}

These observables are not themselves one-point rate observables, yet in the
explicit D-MAP family above they reduce to sharp thresholds in the coordinate
\(\Gamma\).

It is useful to keep the D-MAP record construction in two logically separate
steps.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.2em]
\item The labelled kernels determine the stationary word law, the zero-run
hazard, and the covariance sequence of the visible binary record.
\item Exact \(1\)-dependence for this D-MAP is first equivalent to the scalar
coordinate condition \(\Gamma=\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)\).
That condition is labelled according to \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}:
the inverse theorem gives
\[
\mu_{\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}}=\mu_{\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma}
\quad\text{and hence only}\quad
\{e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau}\}.
\]
Thus, without a supplied branch label, the statement is made on the quotient by
\((\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r})\sim(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma)\).
\end{enumerate}
The constrained D-MAP produces a full-support renewal law.  Its distinguished
record threshold in the main theorem chain is therefore the exact
\(1\)-dependence threshold where the hidden eigenmode vanishes.

\phantomsection\label{tab:signatures}\phantomsection\label{tab:notation-global}
The regime summary and consolidated notation table are in the supplementary
material.  The detailed theorem forms below keep only the symbols needed for the
D-MAP law and proofs.  Throughout the paper \(p\) and \(s\) are reserved for
the two one-bin survival factors in the D-MAP kernel.  Generic quantile
probabilities are denoted by \(q\) or \(q_\alpha\), and diagonal root
candidates are denoted by \(z\).  The vector
\(\Rinc=(r_0,r_1,r_2)\) denotes the three visible inclusion coordinates;
when a numerical rate is needed on the exchange diagonal it is written
\(R_{\rm diag}\), not \(r\).  In the main finite-record proofs, \(K_N\) is the
number of complete retained cycles whose starts lie before the calendar stop,
so the complete-cycle indices are \(0,\ldots,K_N\) when the record begins with
a retained cycle start.  The set \(J_{m,N}\) is the corresponding admissible
all-complete-cycle set for the lag-\(m\) reward after the required endpoint
and look-ahead deletions.  The supplementary diagnostic notation
\(\widehat K_N\) is reserved for raw observed click-time indices before those
retained-cycle deletions are applied.

\begin{definition}[Constrained D-MAP law used by Theorems A--E]\label{def:main-sampled-kernel-law}
Let \(\mu_{\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau}\) denote the stationary
visible binary law generated by the kernel pair in
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.  Equivalently, that pair is
\[
\mathcal K(p,s)=
\left(
T_0=\begin{pmatrix}p&0\\ b&s\end{pmatrix},
\quad
T_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1-p\\0&1-s-b\end{pmatrix}
\right),
\]
where
\[
p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},\qquad
b=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}
\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\,dr .
\]
Equivalently \(a=1-s-b\) is the lower-right one-labelled entry.  This is the
kernel pair derived from the sampled-counter model and fixed by
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Detailed form of Theorem~A: constrained D-MAP record law]\label{prop:main-record-wrapper-detailed}
Let \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) have law
\(\mu_{\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau}\) from
\Cref{def:main-sampled-kernel-law}.  Let \(G\) be the
number of zeros between consecutive ones, and put
\[
\rho=\PP(A_0=1),\qquad
\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=p-b .
\]
Then \((A_n)\) is a full-support renewal process with Palm gap law
\[
g_k=\PP(G=k)=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1,\qquad k\ge0 .
\]
If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then
\[
g_k=
\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
     {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\]
while on the equal-rate diagonal the formula is interpreted by the continuous
limit, equivalently for
\(y=\Gamma\Delta\tau=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\) and \(p=e^{-y}\),
\[
g_k=p^k\bigl((1-p)(1+yk)-yp\bigr).
\]
Writing
\[
S_k=\PP(G\ge k),\qquad h_k=\PP(G=k\mid G\ge k)=g_k/S_k ,
\]
the survival tail, hazard, and hazard increment are explicit.  Off the
equal-rate diagonal,
\[
S_k=
\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\qquad
h_k=
1-\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^{k+1}-\Gamma s^{k+1}}
        {\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k},
\]
and
\[
h_{k+1}-h_k
=
\frac{
  \Gamma\kappa_{\mathrm r}\,
  (p-s)^2\,p^k s^k
}{
  \bigl(\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k\bigr)
  \bigl(\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^{k+1}-\Gamma s^{k+1}\bigr)
}>0 .
\]
On the equal-rate diagonal,
\[
S_k=p^k(1+yk),\qquad
h_k=1-p-\frac{yp}{1+yk},
\qquad
h_{k+1}-h_k=
\frac{y^2p}{(1+yk)(1+y(k+1))}>0 .
\]
Thus the zero-run hazard is strictly increasing.  For every \(n\ge1\),
\[
\gamma_n:=\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_n)
=\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}^{\,n-1}.
\]
The record is exact \(1\)-dependent iff \(\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=0\), and in no
positive parameter case is it a finite-order Markov chain.
\end{proposition}
