\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

The paper gives a closed-form record-law and fixed-setting asymptotic analysis
for one constrained latched killed-leakage sampled-counter D-MAP(2) subfamily.
The visible
record identifies the unordered survival/rate coordinates, not hidden labels
or response-side thermodynamic parameters without external calibration.  The

 succeeded in 421ms:
\begin{paperthm}[Fixed-setting retained-record quotient delta method]\label{thm:finite-record-quotient-delta-main}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~C and suppose the population inverse lies in
the stable quotient chart
\[
r_0>0,\qquad \Delta_{\rm inv}=r_1-r_0^2\ne0 .
\]
For the quotient map \(\Phi\) in Theorem~B,
\[
\sqrt N\{\Phi(\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc})-\Phi(\Rinc)\}
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\sigma),
\qquad
\Sigma_\sigma=D\Phi(\Rinc)\Sigma_rD\Phi(\Rinc)^\top .
\]
For the constrained D-MAP population, \(\Phi(\Rinc)=(p+s,ps)\).  If
\[
\Delta_\sigma=\Phi_1(\Rinc)^2-4\Phi_2(\Rinc)=(p-s)^2>0,
\]
let \(z_-<z_+\) be the sorted roots and let
\(\widehat z_{-,N}<\widehat z_{+,N}\) be the correspondingly sorted roots
formed from \(\Phi(\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc})\).  This ordering is visible and
requires no external physical label.  With
\[
J_{\rm root}=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{z_-}{z_--z_+}&-\dfrac1{z_--z_+}\\[6pt]
\dfrac{z_+}{z_+-z_-}&-\dfrac1{z_+-z_-}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
the label-free root CLT is
\[
\sqrt N
\begin{pmatrix}\widehat z_{-,N}-z_-\\ \widehat z_{+,N}-z_+\end{pmatrix}
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,J_{\rm root}\Sigma_\sigma J_{\rm root}^{\top}\right).
\]
For known design interval \(\Delta\tau\), define the root-ordered rates
\[
\vartheta=
\begin{pmatrix}-\log z_-/\Delta\tau\\-\log z_+/\Delta\tau\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\widehat\vartheta_N=
\begin{pmatrix}-\log\widehat z_{-,N}/\Delta\tau\\
-\log\widehat z_{+,N}/\Delta\tau\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta)
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,J_{\rm rate}\Sigma_\sigma J_{\rm rate}^{\top}),
\qquad
J_{\rm rate}=
\begin{pmatrix}-(\Delta\tau z_-)^{-1}&0\\
0&-(\Delta\tau z_+)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}J_{\rm root}.
\]
Thus the roots identify the unordered survival-factor set \(\{p,s\}\) and
the displayed root ordering gives a canonical, label-free version of the
unordered numerical rate set
\[
\left\{-\frac{\log p}{\Delta\tau},-\frac{\log s}{\Delta\tau}\right\}.
\]
If \(\Delta\tau\) is not supplied as a known design interval, the theorem
identifies only the dimensionless unordered product set
\[
\{-\log p,-\log s\}
=\{\Gamma\Delta\tau,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\},
\]
not numerical rates per unit time.
Only the assignment of the two numerical entries to the physical names
\(\Gamma\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) requires the side-data branch
convention.
\end{paperthm}

 succeeded in 420ms:
\begin{paperthm}[Pointwise exchange-diagonal projection example]\label{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main}
Fix
\[
z_0=\frac12,\qquad \sigma_0=(1,1/4),\qquad
H_{z_0}=\{h\in\mathbb R^2:h_2\le z_0h_1\},
\]
and let \(F=\{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2):\sigma_2\le\sigma_1^2/4\}\).  Suppose the
true population satisfies \(\sigma=\sigma_0\), the printed interval
certificate proves
\(\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma_\sigma(z_0)\}>0.037\), and
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\sigma_N^{\rm raw}-\sigma_0)
\Rightarrow Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\sigma(z_0)).
\]
Let \(\Pi_F\) be the locally unique Euclidean projection, with any fixed
measurable tie rule outside the local neighbourhood, and set
\[
\widehat\sigma_N=\Pi_F(\widehat\sigma_N^{\rm raw}),\qquad
X_N=\sqrt N(\widehat\sigma_N-\sigma_0).
\]
Then
\[
X_N\Rightarrow \Pi_{H_{z_0}}Z .
\]
This theorem is only a pointwise projection example at the preselected point
\(z_0=1/2\).  It defines no statistic for testing, no simulated or limiting
critical value, no confidence region, and no feasible or oracle coverage
claim.  Selection of \(z_0\) from the data and uniformity over \(0<z<1\) are
outside its scope.
\end{paperthm}

 succeeded in 430ms:
\begin{paperthm}[Constrained D-MAP record law]\label{thm:main-record-wrapper}
Let \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) have the stationary visible law generated by the
sampled-counter kernels in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.  Put
\[
p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},\qquad
\rho=\PP(A_0=1),\qquad
\lambda_{\rm hid}=p-b .
\]
Then \((A_n)\) is a full-support renewal process.  If \(G\) is the Palm number
of zeros between consecutive ones, then
\[
g_k=\PP(G=k)=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1{\bf 1},\qquad k\ge0 .
\]
For \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\),
\[
g_k=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
          {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\qquad
S_k=\PP(G\ge k)=
\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}p^k-\Gamma s^k}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\]
with continuous-limit formulas on \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\).  The zero-run
hazard \(h_k=g_k/S_k\) is strictly increasing.  The visible covariance has the
single hidden-mode tail
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_n)=\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid}^{\,n-1},
\qquad n\ge1 .
\]
  The record is exact \(1\)-dependent if and only if
  \(\lambda_{\rm hid}=0\).  Moreover
  \[
  \gamma_1=\rho(a-\rho)<0,
  \]
  so adjacent outputs are not independent and the record is not
  \(0\)-dependent.  In no positive parameter case is it a finite-order Markov
  chain.

330:reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
331-\[

333:\qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,

338-\psi_K(M)=M^{-1}KM,
339-\]

341-\[
342-D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\qquad(B\in\mathfrak g_n).
343-\]
344:Consequently the visible fibre through \(K\) contains, in a neighbourhood of
345:\(K\), a smooth immersed manifold of dimension exactly \((n-1)^2\).  Every
346-kernel on a sufficiently small neighbourhood of this orbit manifold remains
347-strictly substochastic: its entries and killing deficits are positive.  After
348:quotienting by the finite reset-preserving permutation group, the local fibre
349:still has dimension \((n-1)^2\).

388-\begin{remark}[Nonminimal and graph-specific open interfaces]
389-\label{rem:nstate-identifiability-open-interfaces-main}
390-The characterization and the two headline results deliberately assume
391-Hankel/minimal rank \(n\). If a nominal
392-\(n\)-state representation has lower visible rank, equal laws need not be
393:related by an invertible \(n\times n\) similarity; a sharp classification then
394-requires a stratified treatment of nonminimal augmentations. For a fixed
395-nonserial zero pattern on the boundary of the Markovian cone, evaluating the
396-orbit intersection \(\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)\) is an exact semialgebraic
397-problem, but no graph-uniform closed form is claimed here. Finally, collision
398-multiplicity is population-identifiable in the serial model but statistically
399-singular under noisy finite records. These are explicit interfaces, not
400-consequences of the present results.
401-\end{remark}

\begin{paperthm}[Single-record complete visible-law specification test]
\label{thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main}
Fix $0<\varepsilon<M<\infty$, put

\[
\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}=[\varepsilon,M]^2,
\qquad \mathcal P_0=\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}\},
\]

where $P_\theta$ is the stationary visible law of the sampled-counter kernels
at the dimensionless parameter $\theta=(x,y)$.  For a binary word
$w=(w_1,\ldots,w_m)$, write

\[
P_\theta[w]=\pi_\theta T_{w_1}(\theta)\cdots
T_{w_m}(\theta)\mathbf1,
\]

where $\pi_\theta$ is stationary for $T_0(\theta)+T_1(\theta)$.  On
stationary binary laws define

\[
d(P,Q)=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}4^{-m}
\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^m}|P[w]-Q[w]|,
\qquad
d(P,\mathcal P_0)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}d(P,P_\theta).
\]

For a record $A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1}$ with $N\ge3$, let

\[
\widehat P_N[w]=\frac1{N-m+1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-m}
\mathbf1_{\{A_j\cdots A_{j+m-1}=w\}},
\qquad
L_N=\max\left\{3,\left\lfloor\frac18\log_2N\right\rfloor\right\},
\]

and set

\[
d_N=\min_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\sum_{m=1}^{L_N}4^{-m}\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^m}
|\widehat P_N[w]-P_\theta[w]|.
\]

Choose a minimizer $\widehat\theta_N$ by a fixed lexicographic rule.  Delete
the initial and terminal incomplete cycles and denote the remaining complete
zero gaps by $G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}$.  If $g_\theta$ is the model Palm gap
mass function, define

\[
h_\theta(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=1\}}
-\frac{g_\theta(1)}{g_\theta(2)}\mathbf1_{\{k=2\}}.
\]

When $K_N\ge3$, put

\[
\widehat\nu_N=\frac1{K_N}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_j)^2,
\qquad
\widehat I_N=\frac{K_N}{N}\widehat\nu_N^2,
\]

\[
Z_N=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\widehat I_N}}
\sum_{j=1}^{K_N-1}
h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_j)h_{\widehat\theta_N}(G_{j+1}).
\]

If $K_N<3$ or $\widehat I_N=0$, set $Z_N=0$.  Thus, for every binary
record of length $N\ge3$, the test

\[
\varphi_N=\mathbf1_{\{d_N>N^{-1/4}\ \text{or}\ Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}
\tag{F}
\]

is defined without empirical roots, logarithms, or evaluations of the analytic
root chart outside its domain.  It has the following properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Its null size is compact-uniform:
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\varepsilon,M}}
\left|\PP_\theta(\varphi_N=1)-\alpha\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This includes the exchange diagonal and every null triangular array, in
particular arrays satisfying $N^{1/4}|p_N-s_N|=O(1)$.

\item If $P$ is a fixed stationary ergodic binary law and
$d(P,\mathcal P_0)>0$, then
\[
\PP_P(\varphi_N=1)\longrightarrow1.
\]
The convergence is uniform on any class with a common geometric
$\alpha$-mixing envelope $\alpha_P(k)\le Cq^k$, $q<1$, and a common
separation $d(P,\mathcal P_0)\ge\delta>0$.  No consistency assertion is made
for arbitrary stationary nonergodic mixtures.

\item Fix an interior exchange point $\theta_0=(x_0,x_0)$, and abbreviate
$g_k=g_{\theta_0}(k)$, $\mu=\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)g_k$, and
\[
h(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=1\}}-\frac{g_1}{g_2}\mathbf1_{\{k=2\}}.
\]
For $0\le\eta<g_2/g_1$, the transition matrix
\[
Q_\eta(\ell\mid k)=g_\ell\{1+\eta h(k)h(\ell)\}
\tag{G}
\]
is stochastic, has stationary marginal $g$, and defines by Palm inversion a
stationary nonrenewal visible law when $\eta>0$.  This law preserves exactly
the sampled-counter coordinates $r_0,r_1,r_2$, because
\[
r_0=\mu^{-1},\qquad r_1=\mu^{-1}g_0,
\qquad r_2=\mu^{-1}\{g_1+g_0Q_\eta(0\mid0)\},
\]
and $Q_\eta(0\mid0)=g_0$.  Nevertheless,
\[
\PP_\eta(10101)=\mu^{-1}g_1^2(1+\eta),
\]
so a length-five word separates every $\eta>0$ from the renewal null.

\item Put
\[
\nu=\EE_g h(G)^2=g_1+\frac{g_1^2}{g_2},
\qquad \mathcal I=\frac{\nu^2}{\mu}.
\]
Along $\eta_N=t/\sqrt N$, $t\ge0$, the stationary record experiments in
part~\textup{(iii)} satisfy
\[
\log\frac{dP_{\eta_N}^{(N)}}{dP_0^{(N)}}
=t\Delta_N-\frac12t^2\mathcal I+o_{P_0}(1),
\qquad \Delta_N\Rightarrow N(0,\mathcal I).
\]
Moreover, $\widehat I_N\to_P\mathcal I$ and
\[
Z_N\Rightarrow N(t\sqrt{\mathcal I},1),
\qquad
\pi_\alpha(t)=1-\Phi_{\rm N}
\{z_{1-\alpha}-t\sqrt{\mathcal I}\}.
\]
Thus $\pi_\alpha(t)>\alpha$ for every $t>0$.  If
$\eta_N=o(N^{-1/2})$, the Kullback--Leibler divergence tends to zero, while
the score component of \textup{(F)} attains the Neyman--Pearson power envelope
of this one-dimensional Gaussian-shift subexperiment at the $N^{-1/2}$
rate.
\end{enumerate}

The distributional-distance guard in parts~\textup{(i)}--\textup{(ii)} is a
specialization of established stationary-ergodic testing methods
\cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,Ryabko2012StationaryTesting}.  Generic
LAN and Gaussian-shift optimality are also standard
\cite{vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.  The model-specific assertions are
the exchange-uniform finite-range score, the exactly
$(r_0,r_1,r_2)$-preserving alternative \textup{(G)}, and their joint use with
the complete visible-law guard.
\end{paperthm}

\begin{theorem}[Complete Markov--Palm tangent space and pointwise omnibus score]
\label{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}
Fix $0<\alpha<1$, an interior exchange point $\theta_0=(x_0,x_0)$, and let
$g=(g_k)_{k\geq0}$ be its Palm zero-gap law.  Thus $g_k>0$,
$\mu=\sum_{k\geq0}(k+1)g_k<\infty$, and, for this sampled-counter law,
$g$ has an exponential tail.  Put
\[
 \mathsf H=L^2(g\otimes g),\qquad
 \mathsf H_{\rm int}=\{q\in\mathsf H:
 \EE(q\mid G_0)=\EE(q\mid G_1)=0\},
\]
where $G_0,G_1$ are independent with law $g$, and define
\[
 \mathsf T=\{q\in\mathsf H_{\rm int}:q(0,0)=0\}.
 \tag{H}
\]
Consider all quadratic-mean differentiable Markov-gap paths
\[
 Q_t(\ell\mid k)=g_\ell w_t(k,\ell),\qquad w_0=1,
 \qquad \left\|\frac{2(\sqrt{w_t}-1)}t-q\right\|_{\mathsf H}
 \longrightarrow0,
\tag{I}
\]
whose rows sum to one, for which $gQ_t=g$, and which preserve
$(r_0,r_1,r_2)$ to first order.  Then the following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The closed tangent space of these paths is exactly $\mathsf T$; in
particular it is infinite dimensional.  If
\[
 u_0(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=0\}}-g_0,\qquad
 v_0(k,\ell)=u_0(k)u_0(\ell),
\]
then
\[
 \mathsf T=\mathsf H_{\rm int}\ominus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\}.
 \tag{J}
\]
Every $q\in\mathsf T$ is realized by a two-sided path in \textup{(I)} whose
kernels satisfy a Doeblin minorization by $(1-o(1))g$ and preserve $g$ and
all three inclusion coordinates exactly.  A nonzero such path is nonrenewal
for all sufficiently small nonzero $t$.

\item Every adjacent-pair score generated by a quadratic-mean differentiable
renewal marginal path belongs to the closed span of
$s(G_0)+s(G_1)$, with $s\in L^2_0(g)$.  Hence the sampled-counter renewal
nuisance space is orthogonal to $\mathsf T$.  On the ambient space
$\mathsf H$, the efficient information operator for the Markov interaction
is
\[
 \mathcal I_{\rm eff}=\mu^{-1}\Pi_{\mathsf T},
 \tag{K}
\]
where
\[
 \Pi_{\mathsf T}f=f-\EE(f\mid G_0)-\EE(f\mid G_1)+\EE f
 -\frac{\langle f,v_0\rangle_{\mathsf H}}
 {\|v_0\|_{\mathsf H}^2}v_0.
 \tag{L}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \ker\mathcal I_{\rm eff}
 =\mathsf H_{\rm int}^{\perp}\oplus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\},
 \qquad
 \left.\mathcal I_{\rm eff}\right|_{\mathsf T}
 =\mu^{-1}I_{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{M}
\]

\item Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles from a stationary record and
write its complete gaps as $G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}$, where
$K_N/N\to_P\mu^{-1}$.  For $q\in\mathsf T$, let
\[
 \Delta_N(q)=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{K_N-1}q(G_i,G_{i+1}).
\]
For each fixed finite collection $q_1,\ldots,q_d\in\mathsf T$, the null
joint limit is centred Gaussian with covariance
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\operatorname{Cov}
 \{\Delta_N(q_a),\Delta_N(q_b)\}
 =\mu^{-1}\langle q_a,q_b\rangle_{\mathsf H}.
 \tag{N}
\]
Along the realizing paths constructed in part~\textup{(i)}, or any other
such path whose retained-record endpoint log likelihood is $o_{P_0}(1)$,
the score $q$, evaluated at $t_N=N^{-1/2}$, satisfies
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{N,q}}{dP_{N,0}}
 =\Delta_N(q)-\frac1{2\mu}\|q\|_{\mathsf H}^2+o_{P_0}(1).
 \tag{O}
\]
Thus the limit is the isonormal process on $\mathsf T$ with covariance
\textup{(N)}, rather than a $\mathsf T$-valued normal random element with
identity covariance.  No uniform-LAN assertion over arbitrary norm-compact
subsets of $\mathsf T$ is made.

\item Put
\[
 e_0(k)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\{k=0\}}-g_0}{\sqrt{g_0(1-g_0)}}
\]
and choose a bounded orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,\ldots$ of
$L^2_0(g)\cap\{e_0\}^{\perp}$.  Enumerate
\[
 \{e_a\otimes e_b:a,b\geq0,\ (a,b)\neq(0,0)\}
 =\{\phi_1,\phi_2,\ldots\};
\]
this is an orthonormal basis of $\mathsf T$.  Fix strictly positive weights
$\lambda_j$ satisfying
\[
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j<\infty,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2<\infty,
 \tag{P}
\]
and any deterministic $J_N\uparrow\infty$.  Put
\[
 \widehat\mu_N=
 \begin{cases}
 K_N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{K_N}(G_i+1),&K_N\geq1,\\
 1,&K_N=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
and define, when $K_N\geq2$,
\[
 Z_{j,N}=\sqrt{\frac{\widehat\mu_N}{N}}
 \sum_{i=1}^{K_N-1}\phi_j(G_i,G_{i+1}),\qquad
 Q_N=\sum_{j=1}^{J_N}\lambda_jZ_{j,N}^2,
 \tag{Q}
\]
and put $Q_N=0$ otherwise.  If $\zeta_j$ are independent standard normals,
then
\[
 Q_N\Rightarrow Q_0:=\sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j\zeta_j^2.
 \tag{R}
\]
Let $c_{\alpha,\lambda}$ be the $(1-\alpha)$ quantile of $Q_0$.  Under the
local direction $q=\sum_jq_j\phi_j\in\mathsf T$ along one of the paths
admitted in \textup{(O)},
\[
 Q_N\Rightarrow
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j
 \left(\zeta_j+\frac{q_j}{\sqrt\mu}\right)^2.
 \tag{S}
\]
Consequently the test
$\psi_N=\mathbf1_{\{Q_N>c_{\alpha,\lambda}\}}$ has limiting power strictly
larger than $\alpha$ for every fixed $q\in\mathsf T\setminus\{0\}$.

\begin{proposition}[Sharp local-null Helmert coupling boundary]
\label{prop:helmert-growing-layer-sharp-main}
Retain the exchange-point notation of
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}, put
$p_0=e^{-x_0}$, and write
\[
 S_j=\PP_g(G\geq j)=p_0^j(1+x_0j),\qquad j\geq0.
\]
For $j\geq0$ define the weighted Helmert contrast
\[
 e_j(k)=
 \sqrt{\frac{S_{j+1}}{g_jS_j}}\,\mathbf1_{\{k=j\}}
 -\sqrt{\frac{g_j}{S_jS_{j+1}}}\,\mathbf1_{\{k\geq j+1\}}.
 \tag{V}
\]
Thus $e_0$ is the contrast used in
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}, and
$e_0,e_1,\ldots$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0(g)$.  For $J\geq1$ let
\[
 \boldsymbol\Phi_J=
 \bigl(e_a\otimes e_b:0\leq a,b\leq J,\ (a,b)\neq(0,0)\bigr),
 \qquad d_J=(J+1)^2-1,
 \tag{W}
\]
in any fixed order, and let $\mathbf Z_{J,N}$ be the corresponding vector of
scores in \textup{(Q)}, with the basis in \textup{(V)} fixed at $\theta_0$.
Set $n_N=N/\mu$, fix $C<\infty$, and let $\mathcal H_N(C)$ be the physical
sampled-counter null parameters $\sigma$ satisfying
$\|\sqrt N(\sigma-\sigma_0)\|\leq C$, as in \textup{(T)}.  If
$J_N\to\infty$, the following condition is necessary and sufficient:
\[
 n_NS_{J_N}^2\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{X}
\]
More precisely, \textup{(X)} is equivalent to the existence, on extensions of
the probability spaces, of
$\boldsymbol\xi_{N,\sigma}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{d_{J_N}})$ such that, for every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \sup_{\sigma\in\mathcal H_N(C)}
 \PP_\sigma\!\left(
  \|\mathbf Z_{J_N,N}-\boldsymbol\xi_{N,\sigma}\|_2>\varepsilon
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{Y}
\]
In particular, the same equivalence holds at the fixed exchange point
$\sigma_0$.

Replacing the deterministic cycle count by the
calendar stopping index and replacing $\mu$ by $\widehat\mu_N$ contribute,
respectively,
\[
 O_P(J_NN^{-1/4})\quad\hbox{and}\quad O_P(J_NN^{-1/2})
 \tag{Z}
\]
in Euclidean norm.  The local null covariance perturbation contributes
$O_P(J_N^3N^{-1/2})$; all three terms are uniformly $o_P(1)$ under
\textup{(X)}.

The necessity in \textup{(X)} already follows from the fact that a standard
Gaussian limit for the moving corner coordinate
$e_{J_N}\otimes e_{J_N}$ requires
\[
 n_NS_{J_N}^2\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{AA}
\]
More strongly, if some $r_N<J_N$ satisfies
$n_NS_{r_N}^2\to0$ and $J_N-r_N\asymp J_N$, then, with probability tending
to one, every score in the block
\[
 \{e_a\otimes e_b:r_N\leq a,b\leq J_N\}
 \tag{AB}
\]
is zero.  The corresponding standard Gaussian block has
$(J_N-r_N+1)^2$ degrees of freedom, so neither an unweighted chi-square
approximation for that block nor an $o_P(1)$ Euclidean coupling can hold.

In the second-order band
$2x_0J_N=\log n_N+O(\log\log n_N)$, put
\[
 \omega_N=\log n_N+2\log\log n_N-2x_0J_N.
\]
Then \textup{(Y)} holds if and only if $\omega_N\to\infty$.  Equivalently,
the sharp second-order region is
\[
 J_N\leq
 \frac{\log n_N+2\log\log n_N-\omega_N}{2x_0}
 \tag{AC}
\]
for some $\omega_N\to\infty$.

\begin{paperthm}[Fixed-setting retained-record quotient delta method]\label{thm:finite-record-quotient-delta-main}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~C and suppose the population inverse lies in
the stable quotient chart
\[
r_0>0,\qquad \Delta_{\rm inv}=r_1-r_0^2\ne0 .
\]
For the quotient map \(\Phi\) in Theorem~B,
\[
\sqrt N\{\Phi(\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc})-\Phi(\Rinc)\}
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\sigma),
\qquad
\Sigma_\sigma=D\Phi(\Rinc)\Sigma_rD\Phi(\Rinc)^\top .
\]
For the constrained D-MAP population, \(\Phi(\Rinc)=(p+s,ps)\).  If
\[
\Delta_\sigma=\Phi_1(\Rinc)^2-4\Phi_2(\Rinc)=(p-s)^2>0,
\]
let \(z_-<z_+\) be the sorted roots and let
\(\widehat z_{-,N}<\widehat z_{+,N}\) be the correspondingly sorted roots
formed from \(\Phi(\Rinch_N^{\rm cyc})\).  This ordering is visible and
requires no external physical label.  With
\[
J_{\rm root}=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{z_-}{z_--z_+}&-\dfrac1{z_--z_+}\\[6pt]
\dfrac{z_+}{z_+-z_-}&-\dfrac1{z_+-z_-}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
the label-free root CLT is
\[
\sqrt N
\begin{pmatrix}\widehat z_{-,N}-z_-\\ \widehat z_{+,N}-z_+\end{pmatrix}
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,J_{\rm root}\Sigma_\sigma J_{\rm root}^{\top}\right).
\]
For known design interval \(\Delta\tau\), define the root-ordered rates
\[
\vartheta=
\begin{pmatrix}-\log z_-/\Delta\tau\\-\log z_+/\Delta\tau\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\widehat\vartheta_N=
\begin{pmatrix}-\log\widehat z_{-,N}/\Delta\tau\\
-\log\widehat z_{+,N}/\Delta\tau\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\vartheta_N-\vartheta)
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,J_{\rm rate}\Sigma_\sigma J_{\rm rate}^{\top}),
\qquad
J_{\rm rate}=
\begin{pmatrix}-(\Delta\tau z_-)^{-1}&0\\
0&-(\Delta\tau z_+)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}J_{\rm root}.
\]
Thus the roots identify the unordered survival-factor set \(\{p,s\}\) and
the displayed root ordering gives a canonical, label-free version of the
unordered numerical rate set
\[
\left\{-\frac{\log p}{\Delta\tau},-\frac{\log s}{\Delta\tau}\right\}.
\]
If \(\Delta\tau\) is not supplied as a known design interval, the theorem
identifies only the dimensionless unordered product set
\[
\{-\log p,-\log s\}
=\{\Gamma\Delta\tau,\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\},
\]
not numerical rates per unit time.
Only the assignment of the two numerical entries to the physical names
\(\Gamma\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) requires the side-data branch
convention.
\end{paperthm}

 \mathcal N\{h^2\mathcal I(z),\mathcal I(z)\}
\tag{SE11}
\]
uniformly over \(z\in\mathcal K\) and bounded \(h\).
The limit identifies \(h^2\), not the sign of \(h\).  This is the complete
singular experiment for the specified path; it is not an ordered hidden-label
experiment.
\end{maintheorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(x=-\log p\), \(y=-\log s\).  The Palm gap formula in Theorem~A is
\[
 g_{p,s}(k)
 =\frac{y(1-p)p^k-x(1-s)s^k}{y-x},
\tag{SE12}
\]
with its continuous value when \(p=s\).  Substitute \(p=z+d\) and \(s=z-d\)
and expand the even analytic function of \(d\).  The constant and quadratic
coefficients are exactly \textup{(SE2)} and \textup{(SE3)}, proving
\textup{(SE4)}.  The diagonal survival tail is
\[
 S_z(k)=z^k(1-k\log z).
\]
Thus \(g_z(k)=S_z(k)-S_z(k+1)\), which proves the first identity in
\textup{(SE2)} and, by summing the tails, the formula for \(\mu_z\).
Differentiating \(\sum_kg_{z+d,z-d}(k)=1\) at order \(d^2\) gives
\(\sum_kB_z(k)=0\), hence the centring in \textup{(SE5)}.

On every \(\mathcal K\Subset(0,1)\), the masses in \textup{(SE12)} and all
their derivatives through any fixed order have a common
\(C(1+k)^m r^k\) envelope for some \(r<1\).  Termwise differentiation and
summation are therefore valid uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).  Formula
\textup{(SE3)} gives \(|b_z(k)|\le C_{\mathcal K}(1+k)^2\), so
\textup{(SE6)} is finite and continuous.  It is positive: if it vanished,
then \(B_z(k)=0\) for every \(k\).  But
\[
 B_z(0)=-\frac{2\log z+3}{6z};
\]
its only zero is \(z=e^{-3/2}\), and at that point the numerator in
\textup{(SE3)} for \(k=1\) equals \(-6z\), so \(B_z(1)\ne0\).

Put \(q=d^2\).  Uniform analytic differentiation in the symmetric coordinate
\((p+s,ps)=(2z,z^2-q)\) gives
\[
 g_{z+\sqrt q,z-\sqrt q}(k)
 =g_z(k)\{1+qb_z(k)+q^2c_z(k)+q^3R_{z,q}(k)\},
\tag{SE13}
\]
where \(\sum_kg_z(k)c_z(k)=0\) and \(c_z,R_{z,q}\) have common polynomial
envelopes on \(\mathcal K\) for \(q\) in a fixed right neighbourhood of zero.
The same statement follows directly from \textup{(SE12)}.  Uniform
exponential gap tails imply
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le K_N}G_{j,N}=O_{P_{N,z,0}}(\log N)
\tag{SE14}
\]
uniformly in \(z\in\mathcal K\).  Taylor expansion of the logarithm in
\textup{(SE13)}, on the event in \textup{(SE14)}, therefore gives uniformly
for \(|h|\le H\), with \(q=h^2N^{-1/2}\),
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\log
\frac{g_{z+\sqrt q,z-\sqrt q}(G_{j,N})}{g_z(G_{j,N})}
={}&h^2\Delta_{N,z}\\
&+\frac{h^4}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
\{c_z(G_{j,N})-\tfrac12b_z(G_{j,N})^2\}+o_P(1).
\end{split}
\tag{SE15}
\]

Under the diagonal law the complete Palm gaps are consecutive i.i.d.
variables with mass \(g_z\), and the renewal count satisfies
\(K_N/N\to1/\mu_z\).  The uniform regenerative law of large numbers applied
to the two polynomially bounded rewards in \textup{(SE15)} makes its second
line converge to \(-h^4\mathcal I(z)/2\), uniformly on
\(\mathcal K\times[-H,H]\).  The uniform regenerative central limit theorem
applied to \(b_z\) proves \textup{(SE8)}.  Both results can also be obtained by
the subsequence criterion: every sequence \(z_N\in\mathcal K\) has a
convergent subsequence, and the common exponential envelope supplies
Lindeberg, renewal-count replacement, and uniform integrability along that
subsequence.

It remains to compare the product of complete-gap likelihoods with the
stationary \(N\)-bin likelihood.  Their ratio contains only the left
equilibrium-delay factor, the right censored-tail factor, and the normalizing
cycle mean.  Their logarithmic \(q\)-derivatives have polynomial envelopes in
the two endpoint lengths.  Those lengths are \(O_P(\log N)\) uniformly by the
same exponential-tail bound, so their total log-likelihood contribution is
\(O_P(N^{-1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N)=o_P(1)\).  This proves
\textup{(SE9)}.

The right side of \textup{(SE9)} is a continuous function of \(h\) and the
remainder is uniform on the compact index set.  Hence the likelihood-ratio
processes converge in \(C([-H,H])\) to
\[
 h\longmapsto
 \exp\{h^2\sqrt{\mathcal I(z)}\,Z-\tfrac12h^4\mathcal I(z)\},
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
which is \textup{(SE10)}.  Le Cam's third lemma gives \textup{(SE11)}.
Finally,
\[
\sqrt N\{(p_{N,z,h}+s_{N,z,h},p_{N,z,h}s_{N,z,h})
-(2z,z^2)\}=(0,-h^2),
\]
which explains both the \(N^{-1/4}\) scale and the loss of the sign.  General
locally conic and loss-of-identifiability asymptotics are established in
\cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,
LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}; the calculation above is the
compact-uniform stationary-renewal specialization.
\end{proof}

 succeeded in 237ms:

\item The null calibration in \textup{(R)} is stable along the exchange
boundary in the following explicit local sense.  Let
$\sigma=(p+s,ps)$ be the symmetric sampled-counter coordinate and, for fixed
$C<\infty$, let $\sigma_N$ range over null sequences satisfying
\[
 \|\sqrt N(\sigma_N-\sigma_0)\|\leq C.
 \tag{T}
\]
Use in \textup{(Q)} the basis fixed at $\sigma_0$ and the displayed
$\widehat\mu_N$.  Then
\[
 \sup_{\sigma_N:\,\textup{(T)}}
 \left|\PP_{\sigma_N}(Q_N>c_{\alpha,\lambda})-\alpha\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{U}
\]
This class includes exchange-root splittings
$N^{1/4}|p_N-s_N|=O(1)$ provided their symmetric coordinates obey
\textup{(T)}.
\end{enumerate}

The algebraic assertions in parts~\textup{(i)}--\textup{(ii)} use only full
support of $g$, finite $\mu$, and square-integrability of each local score.
For the explicit realizing paths, the uniform density-ratio bound controls
the endpoint terms in parts~\textup{(iii)}--\textup{(iv)}.  The
sampled-counter exponential tail and analytic dependence on $\sigma$ are used
in part~\textup{(v)} for its uniform triangular-array statement.  No claim
that finite mean alone controls the endpoints of every quadratic-mean
differentiable stationary-record path is made.

Generic basis tests of serial independence, Hilbert-space central limit
theorems, and Gaussian-shift arguments are established methods
\cite{SkaugTjostheim1993SerialIndependence,
DedeckerMerlevede2003HilbertCLT,vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
The assertions here are restricted to the sampled-counter Markov--Palm
interaction: the additional atom constraint in \textup{(H)}, its information
projection, and the exchange-boundary calibration of \textup{(Q)}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The row and stationary-marginal identities for \textup{(I)} are
\[
 \sum_\ell g_\ell w_t(k,\ell)=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_k g_kw_t(k,\ell)=1.
\]
Differentiating in quadratic mean gives the two conditional-mean constraints
in \textup{(H)}.  Fixed $g$ fixes $r_0=\mu^{-1}$ and
$r_1=\mu^{-1}g_0$, whereas a stationary Markov gap law satisfies
\[
 r_2=\mu^{-1}\{g_1+g_0Q_t(0\mid0)\}.
\]
Since point evaluation at $(0,0)$ is continuous in $\mathsf H$,
$Q_t(0\mid0)=g_0\{1+tq(0,0)+o(t)\}$; hence preservation of $r_2$ to first
order is equivalent to $q(0,0)=0$.

For $q\in\mathsf H_{\rm int}$, direct expansion and double centring give
\[
 \langle q,v_0\rangle_{\mathsf H}=g_0^2q(0,0),
\]
which proves \textup{(J)} and \textup{(L)}.  To prove realizability, truncate
$q$ at levels $m$ and write
$q_m=\Pi_{\mathsf T}\{(-m)\vee(q\wedge m)\}$.  Then $q_m$ is bounded and
$q_m\to q$ in $\mathsf H$.  Choose $m(t)\uparrow\infty$ so slowly that
$|t|\|q_{m(t)}\|_\infty\to0$ and set
$w_t=1+tq_{m(t)}$.  Its weighted row and column sums are exactly one and
$w_t(0,0)=1$; hence all three inclusion coordinates are exact.  Moreover,
$Q_t(\ell\mid k)\geq\{1-o(1)\}g_\ell$, proving the Doeblin assertion.  If
a nonzero score generated a renewal kernel, it would have the form
$a(\ell)$; the two centring identities would then force $a=0$.
The inequality
\[
 \left|2\{\sqrt{1+x}-1\}-x\right|\leq Cx^2,
 \qquad |x|\leq\tfrac12,
\]
together with $|t|\|q_{m(t)}\|_\infty\to0$ proves the quadratic-mean
differentiability in \textup{(I)}.

The Hoeffding row--column decomposition of $L^2(g\otimes g)$ is
\[
 \mathbb R\oplus L^2_0(G_0)\oplus L^2_0(G_1)
 \oplus\mathsf H_{\rm int}.
\]
A renewal marginal perturbation contributes only its one-gap score at the two
ends of an adjacent pair.  It is therefore orthogonal to $\mathsf T$.
Under the null, successive interaction rewards have zero lag-one covariance:
\[
 \EE\{q_a(G_0,G_1)q_b(G_1,G_2)\}=0.
\]
The number of complete cycles per calendar bin tends to $\mu^{-1}$, so the
information quadratic form is $\mu^{-1}\|q\|_{\mathsf H}^2$.  Projection
onto the admissible interaction scores proves \textup{(K)}--\textup{(M)}.

For each fixed finite collection of scores, the one-dependent central limit
theorem and random-index replacement prove \textup{(N)}.  For the realizing
paths in part~\textup{(i)}, the bound
$|t|\|q_{m(t)}\|_\infty\to0$ also makes the endpoint log likelihood
negligible.  Quadratic-mean differentiability then gives \textup{(O)}; the
same conclusion holds under the alternative endpoint hypothesis stated in
part~\textup{(iii)}.  This proves the finite-dimensional local experiment.
Identity covariance on the
infinite-dimensional space is not trace class, so the limit can only be
interpreted cylindrically as the displayed isonormal process.

The normalized $e_0$ is proportional to $u_0$.  Tensoring an orthonormal
basis of $L^2_0(g)$ gives an orthonormal basis of
$\mathsf H_{\rm int}$, and deleting $e_0\otimes e_0$ imposes \textup{(J)}.
Condition \textup{(P)} makes
\[
 \bigl(\sqrt{\lambda_j}\phi_j(G_i,G_{i+1})\bigr)_{j\geq1}
\]
a square-integrable, one-dependent $\ell^2$-valued random variable.  Its
lag-one covariance vanishes by double centring.  The Hilbert-space central
limit theorem, random-index replacement, and truncation in $J_N$ therefore
give \textup{(R)}.  Joint convergence with the likelihood score and the third
lemma give \textup{(S)}.  If $q\neq0$, some $q_j\neq0$; for every positive
threshold the square of a normal with nonzero mean strictly stochastically
dominates a central normal square.  Conditioning on the remaining independent
coordinates proves strict power because every $\lambda_j$ is positive.

It remains to prove the uniform calibration in \textup{(U)}.  We give the
truncation argument because covariance convergence alone is not a
triangular-array Hilbert-space CLT.  Write
\[
 g_N=g_{\sigma_N},\qquad \delta_N=g_N-g .
\]
Analyticity in the symmetric coordinate and the locally uniform exponential
tail give, uniformly under \textup{(T)},
\[
 \|\delta_N\|_1=O(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \mu_N-\mu=O(N^{-1/2}),
\tag{U1}
\]
together with a common exponential moment for the gap laws \(g_N\).
Introduce the weighted feature
\[
 \Psi(k,\ell)=
 \bigl(\sqrt{\lambda_j}\phi_j(k,\ell)\bigr)_{j\ge1}\in\ell^2,
\qquad
 B_\lambda^2=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2<\infty .
\tag{U2}
\]
Thus \(\|\Psi(k,\ell)\|_{\ell^2}\le B_\lambda\) for every pair.  Since every
\(\phi_j\) is double centred under \(g\),
\[
\begin{split}
 m_N:=\EE_{g_N\otimes g_N}\Psi
 &=\sum_{j\ge1}\sqrt{\lambda_j}
 \langle\phi_j,\delta_N\otimes\delta_N\rangle\,\mathbf e_j,\\
 \|m_N\|_{\ell^2}
 &\le B_\lambda\|\delta_N\|_1^2=O(N^{-1}).
\end{split}
\tag{U3}
\]
This displays, rather than assumes, the cancellation of the two first-order
marginal terms.

Fix \(J\).  The first \(J\) coordinates of
\(\Psi(G_i,G_{i+1})-m_N\) form a uniformly bounded one-dependent triangular
array.  Its lag-zero covariance tends to
\(\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_J)\), while its two lag-one
covariances tend to zero: at \(g\) they vanish exactly by double centring, and
\textup{(U1)} controls the perturbation.  The fixed-dimensional
one-dependent triangular-array CLT therefore gives
\[
 (Z_{1,N},\ldots,Z_{J,N})
 \Longrightarrow(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_J)
\tag{U4}
\]
uniformly under \textup{(T)}.  For completeness, uniformity follows by the
subsequence criterion: from every sequence satisfying \textup{(T)}, extract
a convergent subsequence of
\(\sqrt N(\sigma_N-\sigma_0)\); boundedness gives Lindeberg, \textup{(U1)}
gives the covariance limit, and the usual even--odd blocking proves the
one-dependent CLT.  The uniform renewal law of large numbers replaces the
deterministic number of pairs by \(K_N-1\), and
\(\widehat\mu_N-\mu_N=o_P(1)\).  These replacements are uniform because the
common exponential moment controls both endpoint cycles and the renewal-count
deviation.  The mean contribution in \textup{(U3)} is
\(O(\sqrt N\,\|m_N\|_{\ell^2})=o(1)\).

The passage from fixed \(J\) to the full statistic is also uniform.  Put
\[
 L_J=\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0 .
\]
The even--odd maximal inequality for the centred one-dependent tail feature,
followed by the renewal-count bound \(K_N\le N\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\sigma_N:\,\textup{(T)}}
 \EE_{\sigma_N}\!\left[
 \sum_{j>J}\lambda_jZ_{j,N}^2;\,
 K_N\ge2\right]
 \le C L_J+o(1).
\tag{U5}
\]
Here the \(o(1)\) contains the squared mean from \textup{(U3)} and the event
on which \(\widehat\mu_N\) is outside a fixed compact interval.  The latter
event is exponentially small by the common exponential renewal bound; on its
complement \(\widehat\mu_N\) is uniformly bounded.  This proves
\textup{(U5)} without treating the random number of overlapping pairs as a
conditionally binomial count.

For the limit variable,
\[
 \EE\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\zeta_j^2
 =\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\longrightarrow0.
\tag{U6}
\]
Equations \textup{(U4)}--\textup{(U6)} and Markov's inequality give uniform
bounded-Lipschitz convergence of \(Q_N\) to
\(Q_0=\sum_j\lambda_j\zeta_j^2\).  The law of \(Q_0\) is continuous because
\(\lambda_1>0\), so evaluation at \(c_{\alpha,\lambda}\) proves
\textup{(U)}.  Finally,
\[
 (p_N+s_N,p_Ns_N)
 =(2z,z^2-h^2N^{-1/2}),
\]
so the stated \(N^{-1/4}\) root-splitting sequences satisfy \textup{(T)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Sharp local-null Helmert coupling boundary]

 succeeded in 229ms:
\begin{proposition}[Recalled orbit-fibre consequence of minimal realization]
\label{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main}
Fix \(n\ge2\), put \(\beta=e_n^\top\), and let
\[
\mathcal K_n=\{K\in\RR^{n\times n}:K\ge0,\ K\mathbf1\le\mathbf1,\
\operatorname{spr}(K)<1\}.
\]
For \(K\in\mathcal K_n\), define the killed-reset D-MAP by
\[
T_0=K,\qquad T_1=(I-K)\mathbf1\beta
\]
and its Palm survival coordinates by \(S_k(K)=\beta K^k\mathbf1\).
Call \(K\) minimal when both
\[
\mathcal C(K)=[\,\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1\,],
\qquad
\mathcal O(K)=
\begin{bmatrix}\beta\\ \beta K\\ \vdots\\ \beta K^{n-1}\end{bmatrix}
\]
have rank \(n\). Let
\[
\mathcal G_n=\{M\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\RR):
M\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ \beta M=\beta\},
\]
and let \(\mathfrak P_n\subset\mathcal G_n\) be the reset-preserving
permutation matrices.

For any declared subclass \(\mathcal C\subset\mathcal K_n\) of minimal
kernels, fix the structural equivalence \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) under which
identification is requested, and assume that \(K\sim_{\mathcal C}L\) implies
equality of visible laws. Examples are reset-preserving hidden-state
relabeling and, in a serial rate chart, permutation of the rate coordinates.
Define the Markovian orbit fibre
\[
\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=
\left\{M^{-1}KM\in\mathcal C:M\in\mathcal G_n\right\}
\big/\!\sim_{\mathcal C}.
\]
Then standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the following exact
characterization.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Two minimal kernels \(K,L\in\mathcal K_n\) generate the same stationary
visible click law if and only if
\[
\begin{aligned}
L&=M^{-1}KM &&\text{for the unique }M\in\mathcal G_n\\
&&&\text{implementing their normalized minimal realizations}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\item Equivalently, the declared hidden object is identifiable from the visible law within
\(\mathcal C\), modulo \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\), if and only if
\[
\#\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=1\qquad\text{for every }K\in\mathcal C.
\]
Pointwise identifiability at \(K\) is equivalent to the same condition at
that \(K\); if the cardinality exceeds one, its distinct classes are exactly
the hidden nonidentifiability fibre. Thus this assertion is the orbit-fibre
reformulation of part \textup{(i)}.
\end{enumerate}
Part~\textup{(ii)} is deliberately recorded only as terminology: after the
fibre has been defined, singleton fibre and identifiability modulo
\(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) are the same assertion.  Neither part is claimed as a
new realization theorem.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Deterministic reset makes the visible process renewal. Its Palm gap tail is
exactly \(S_k(K)\), so equality of visible stationary laws is equivalent to
equality of all the scalar coordinates \(\beta K^k\mathbf1\), \(k\ge0\).
Apply the minimal-realization theorem stated above to the triples
\((\beta,K,\mathbf1)\) and \((\beta,L,\mathbf1)\). Its hypotheses are exactly
the two displayed rank conditions in the proposition, and it gives a unique
similarity \(L=M^{-1}KM\). Preservation of the fixed input and output vectors
gives \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\beta M=\beta\), respectively.
Conversely, these two identities give
\[
\beta(M^{-1}KM)^k\mathbf1=\beta K^k\mathbf1
\]
for every \(k\), proving (i). Taking the intersection with
\(\mathcal C\) and then quotienting precisely the declared structural
equivalence proves
the necessary-and-sufficient assertion (ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put \(K=T_0\),
\(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), and
\[
 I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
\]
Then \(K\) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
\(\mathcal K_2\) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
\[
 \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
 \qquad
 K(q)=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
 bq & s+b(1-q)
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{F1}
\]
Here complete means that every \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same stationary
visible click law as \(K\) is \(K(q)\) for exactly one \(q\in I_\ast\).
Writing \(T_0(\alpha,\eta)\) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
rate \(\alpha\) and recovery rate \(\eta\), the endpoints are the two physical
triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
\[
 K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
 \qquad
 K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
 \tag{F2}
\]
If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every \(q\) strictly between the
endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then \(I_\ast=\{1\}\), so
the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First \(b>0\).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
the defining integral gives
\[
 b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
 \qquad
 b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
          =bq_\ast>0.
 \tag{F3}
\]
The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
\(p=s\), \(b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0\), and \(q_\ast=1\).  Consequently
\[
 \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
 \qquad
 \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
\]
so \(K\) is minimal.

Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
\[
 M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
\]
Multiplication, using \(b+s-p=bq_\ast\), gives
\(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)\) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since \(K\) is minimal, its scalar
Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same visible
law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
\(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)\) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
\(L\) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
forces every such \(L\) to have the displayed form.  If
\(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\), its lower-left entry
is \(bq\ge0\).  Invertibility excludes \(q=0\), hence \(q>0\).  Its
upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
\[
 \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
 \tag{F4}
\]

Conversely, let \(q\in I_\ast\).  The two diagonal entries in
\textup{(F1)} are affine in \(q\), with endpoint values \(p,s\) and \(s,p\),
respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
\(a=1-b-s>0\), the two killing deficits are
\[
 \mathbf1-K(q)\mathbf1
 =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
 \tag{F5}
\]
Similarity preserves the spectral radius
\(\max\{p,s\}<1\), so \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\).  This proves that the
displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
entry is \(bq\).

At \(q=1\) one recovers \(K\).  At \(q=q_\ast\),
\[
 K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that \(bq_\ast\) is precisely the no-click
recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
row has the same killing deficit \(a\); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
\(q_\ast\ne1\), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
inside \(I_\ast\) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
and both deficits are already strict there.  If \(q_\ast=1\),
\textup{(F4)} forces \(q=1\).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
identifiability statements follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-collision serial identifiability]
\label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates
\(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed. Let
\[
Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
\]
with all other entries zero, and put
\[
T_0(\theta)=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
T_1(\theta)=(I-T_0(\theta))\mathbf1e_n^\top.
\]
Then the visible record identifies exactly the unordered rate multiset
\(\{\!\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\}\!\}\). Equivalently, the fibre of the
labelled serial parameter is its \(\mathfrak S_n\)-permutation orbit.

More explicitly, if the distinct rates are
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) with multiplicities
\(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the Palm tail
has the confluent Prony form
\[
S_k=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,\qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0,
\]
and its minimal recurrence polynomial is
\[
\chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
\]
The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
\((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible; hence
\(S_0,\ldots,S_{2n-1}\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), including all collision
multiplicities. Pole collision therefore changes conditioning and the local
root chart, but does not change population identifiability.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Starting in phase \(n\), the absorption time is
\(W=X_n+\cdots+X_1\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials with
rates \(\theta_i\). Its Laplace transform is
\[
\EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
=\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}{s}
\]
has at
\(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\). Partial-fraction inversion and
sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give the displayed exponential-polynomial form
with nonzero top confluent coefficient. Standard confluent Prony algebra
then gives the exact minimal annihilator \(\chi_\theta\)
\cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.

For completeness of the finite-coordinate assertion, the matrices
\(\mathcal O(Q)\) and \(\mathcal C(Q)\) are nonsingular: successive rows
\(e_n^\top Q^j\) and successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\) expose the nonzero
bidiagonal products triangularly. Because the exponential is injective on
the real spectrum of \(Q\), Hermite interpolation supplies a polynomial
\(p\) with \(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\); hence the corresponding observation and
reachability spaces for \(T_0=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are also full. Therefore
\[
(S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(T_0)\mathcal C(T_0)
\]
is invertible, and the first \(2n\) tails solve uniquely for the order-\(n\)
recurrence. The roots and their algebraic multiplicities recover
\(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\). Conversely, permuting
the independent summands does not change \(W\), the Palm gap law, or the
stationary renewal law. This proves the exact fibre claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative interior fibre dimension and positivity persistence]
\label{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}
For the unrestricted class with \(\sim_{\mathcal K_n}\) equal to
reset-preserving state relabelling, the hidden kernel is locally
nonidentifiable at every minimal interior point \(K\), where interior means
\(K>0\) and \((I-K)\mathbf1>0\) entrywise. More precisely, the
reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
\[
\mathfrak g_n=\{B:B\mathbf1=0,\ \beta B=0\},
\qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,
\]
and the orbit map
\[
\psi_K:\mathcal G_n\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{n\times n},\qquad
\psi_K(M)=M^{-1}KM,
\]
has injective differential
\[
D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\qquad(B\in\mathfrak g_n).
\]
Consequently the visible fibre through \(K\) contains, in a neighbourhood of
\(K\), a smooth immersed manifold of dimension exactly \((n-1)^2\).  Every
kernel on a sufficiently small neighbourhood of this orbit manifold remains
strictly substochastic: its entries and killing deficits are positive.  After
quotienting by the finite reset-preserving permutation group, the local fibre
still has dimension \((n-1)^2\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because \(\beta\mathbf1=1\),
\(\RR^n=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\oplus\ker\beta\).  Relative to this
decomposition, \(B\mathbf1=0\) removes the first block column and
\(\beta B=0\) forces the range into \(\ker\beta\).  Thus
\(B=\operatorname{diag}(0,A)\), with arbitrary
\(A\in\operatorname{End}(\ker\beta)\), and
\(\dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2\).

Differentiating \(\exp(-tB)K\exp(tB)\) at zero gives
\(D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\).  Suppose \([K,B]=0\).  Since \(B\mathbf1=0\),
\[
BK^j\mathbf1=K^jB\mathbf1=0,
\qquad j=0,\ldots,n-1.
\]
The reachability matrix
\([\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1]\) has rank \(n\), so these
equalities imply \(B=0\).  Hence the differential is injective on all of
\(\mathfrak g_n\), not merely in one selected direction.

The constant-rank theorem now makes the image of \(\psi_K\) near the identity
a smooth immersed manifold of dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For every
\(M\in\mathcal G_n\),
\[
\beta\psi_K(M)^j\mathbf1=\beta K^j\mathbf1\qquad(j\ge0),
\]
so the recalled orbit-fibre result places this entire manifold in the visible
fibre.  Finally, all entries of \(M^{-1}KM\) and all components of
\((I-M^{-1}KM)\mathbf1\) depend continuously on \(M\).  Their values at
\(M=I\) are strictly positive; a sufficiently small identity neighbourhood
therefore remains inside the interior Markovian cone.  The stabilizer has zero
Lie algebra by injectivity of the differential, and quotienting by the finite
reset-preserving permutation group cannot change local dimension.  This proves
all assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Nonminimal and graph-specific open interfaces]
\label{rem:nstate-identifiability-open-interfaces-main}
The characterization and the two headline results deliberately assume
Hankel/minimal rank \(n\). If a nominal
\(n\)-state representation has lower visible rank, equal laws need not be
related by an invertible \(n\times n\) similarity; a sharp classification then
requires a stratified treatment of nonminimal augmentations. For a fixed
nonserial zero pattern on the boundary of the Markovian cone, evaluating the
orbit intersection \(\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)\) is an exact semialgebraic
problem, but no graph-uniform closed form is claimed here. Finally, collision
multiplicity is population-identifiable in the serial model but statistically
singular under noisy finite records. These are explicit interfaces, not
consequences of the present results.
\end{remark}

import unittest

import numpy as np

from artifacts import verify_nstate_identifiability as verify


class SerialKilledLeakageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_endpoints_are_rate_swaps(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        delta = 0.8
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        endpoint_kernels = (
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, lower),
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, upper),
        )
        physical_endpoints = (
            verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta),
            verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(recovery, gamma, delta),
        )
        for expected in physical_endpoints:
            self.assertTrue(
                any(
                    np.allclose(actual, expected, atol=2e-13)
                    for actual in endpoint_kernels
                )
            )

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_interior_is_positive_and_visible_equivalent(
        self,
    ):
        gamma = 2.1
        recovery = 0.9
        delta = 0.6
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        q = 0.35 * lower + 0.65 * upper
        baseline = verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
        interior = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, q)
        self.assertGreater(float(interior.min()), 0.0)
        deficits = np.ones(2) - interior @ np.ones(2)
        self.assertGreater(float(deficits.min()), 0.0)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(interior, 30),
            verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(baseline, 30),
            rtol=2e-12,
            atol=2e-13,
        )

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_collapses_exactly_on_exchange_diagonal(
        self,
    ):
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(1.3, 1.3)
        self.assertEqual(lower, 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(upper, 1.0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(1.3, 1.3, 0.7, 1.0 + 1e-5)

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_rejects_points_beyond_exact_arc(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, 1.0, lower - 1e-6)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, 1.0, upper + 1e-6)

    def test_exact_three_inclusion_image_equation(self):
        examples = (
            (0.35, 0.8, 0.2),
            (0.7, 1.6, 1.0),
            (2.0, 2.0, 1.0),
            (4.0, 0.45, 0.7),
        )
        for gamma, recovery, delta in examples:
            inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            residual = verify.physical_image_residual(inclusions)
            self.assertLess(abs(residual), 2e-12)

    def test_physical_image_equation_detects_intensity_perturbation(self):
        inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(0.7, 1.6, 1.0)
        perturbed = inclusions.copy()
        perturbed[0] *= 1.01
        self.assertGreater(abs(verify.physical_image_residual(perturbed)), 1e-4)

    def test_hidden_mode_obeys_sharp_global_bound(self):
        grid = np.geomspace(1e-4, 50.0, 181)
        values = np.array(
            [verify.hidden_mode_secant(x, y) for x in grid for y in grid]
        )
        self.assertGreaterEqual(float(values.min()), -np.exp(-2.0) - 2e-14)
        self.assertLess(float(values.max()), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            verify.hidden_mode_secant(2.0, 2.0), -np.exp(-2.0), places=15
        )

    def test_small_sampling_interval_mean_expansion_has_sixth_order_remainder(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        normalized_errors = []
        for delta in (0.2, 0.1, 0.05):
            exact = delta * verify.mean_cycle_length(gamma, recovery, delta)
            approximation = verify.small_delta_mean_expansion(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            normalized_errors.append(abs(exact - approximation) / delta**6)
        self.assertLess(max(normalized_errors), 2e-3)

    def test_kernels_are_stochastic_and_clicks_reset(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            t0, t1 = verify.serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
            np.testing.assert_allclose((t0 + t1).sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-13)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t0.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t1.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(t1[:, :-1], 0.0, atol=1e-14))

    def test_hankel_pencil_recovers_unordered_sampled_poles(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 2 * len(rates))
            recovered = verify.recover_sampled_poles(tails, len(rates))
            expected = np.sort(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates)))
            np.testing.assert_allclose(recovered, expected, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-11)

    def test_confluent_recurrence_recovers_collision_multiplicities(self):
        examples = (
            (0.7, 0.7),

            (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3),

            np.testing.assert_allclose(
                polynomial, expected, rtol=2e-8, atol=2e-10

    def test_visible_moments_are_permutation_invariant(self):

        baseline = verify.visible_click_moments(rates, 7)
        permuted = verify.visible_click_moments((1.8, 0.45, 0.95), 7)

    def test_stochastic_similarity_changes_kernel_not_visible_law(self):
        examples = ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3), (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3))

    def test_reset_preserving_similarity_tangent_has_expected_dimension(self):

            for tangent in basis:
                np.testing.assert_allclose(tangent @ np.ones(n_states), 0.0)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(reset @ tangent, 0.0)

def _analytic_h_and_derivative(w: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return H(w) and H'(w) on the real analytic branch w < 1."""
    if not math.isfinite(w) or w >= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("w must be finite and less than one")
    if abs(w) < 1e-6:
        value = 1.0 - w / 3.0 - 4.0 * w**2 / 45.0 - 44.0 * w**3 / 945.0
        derivative = -1.0 / 3.0 - 8.0 * w / 45.0 - 44.0 * w**2 / 315.0
        return value, derivative
    if w > 0.0:
        root = math.sqrt(w)
        angle = math.atanh(root)
        value = root / angle
        derivative = (angle - root / (1.0 - root**2)) / (
            2.0 * root * angle**2
        )
        return value, derivative
    root = math.sqrt(-w)
    angle = math.atan(root)
    value = root / angle
    derivative = -(angle - root / (1.0 + root**2)) / (
        2.0 * root * angle**2
    )
    return value, derivative


def analytic_log_divided_difference(sigma1: float, sigma2: float) -> float:
    """Evaluate the real analytic continuation in symmetric coordinates."""
    if not (math.isfinite(sigma1) and math.isfinite(sigma2)):
        raise ValueError("symmetric coordinates must be finite")
    if sigma1 <= 0.0 or sigma2 <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("sigma1 and sigma2 must be positive")
    w = 1.0 - 4.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**2
    h, _ = _analytic_h_and_derivative(w)
    return 0.5 * sigma1 * (1.0 - 0.5 * math.log(sigma2) * h)


def _analytic_log_divided_difference_gradient(
    sigma1: float, sigma2: float
) -> FloatArray:
    w = 1.0 - 4.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**2
    h, h_prime = _analytic_h_and_derivative(w)
    log_sigma2 = math.log(sigma2)
    dw_dsigma1 = 8.0 * sigma2 / sigma1**3
    dw_dsigma2 = -4.0 / sigma1**2
    common = 1.0 - 0.5 * log_sigma2 * h
    d_sigma1 = 0.5 * common - 0.25 * sigma1 * log_sigma2 * h_prime * dw_dsigma1
    d_sigma2 = -0.25 * sigma1 * (
        h / sigma2 + log_sigma2 * h_prime * dw_dsigma2
    )
    return np.array([d_sigma1, d_sigma2])


def constraint_jacobian(coordinates: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the Jacobian of (analytic image residual, discriminant)."""
    r0, r1, r2 = np.asarray(coordinates, dtype=float)
    denominator = r1 - r0**2
    if r0 <= 0.0 or denominator == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("coordinates lie outside the quotient chart")
    a = r1 / r0
    lam = (r2 - r0**2) / denominator
    sigma1 = 1.0 - a + lam
    sigma2 = r0 * (1.0 - lam) - a + lam
    da = np.array([-r1 / r0**2, 1.0 / r0, 0.0])
    dlam = np.array(
        [2.0 * r0 * (lam - 1.0) / denominator, -lam / denominator, 1.0 / denominator]
    )
    dphi1 = -da + dlam
    dphi2 = np.array([1.0 - lam, 0.0, 0.0]) - da + (1.0 - r0) * dlam
    dphi = np.vstack([dphi1, dphi2])
    gradient = _analytic_log_divided_difference_gradient(sigma1, sigma2)
    de = da + gradient @ dphi
    ddiscriminant = np.array([2.0 * sigma1, -4.0]) @ dphi
    return np.vstack([de, ddiscriminant])


def _gap_masses(x: float, y: float, tolerance: float = 1e-15) -> FloatArray:
    masses: list[float] = []
    p = math.exp(-x)
    s = math.exp(-y)

    def survival(k: int) -> float:
        if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
            theta = 0.5 * (x + y)
            return math.exp(-theta * k) * (1.0 + theta * k)
        return (y * p**k - x * s**k) / (y - x)

    previous = survival(0)
    for k in range(1_000_000):
        following = survival(k + 1)
        masses.append(previous - following)
        if following < tolerance:
            return np.asarray(masses)
        previous = following
    raise ArithmeticError("gap-law truncation did not converge")


def survival_factor_gap_masses(p: float, s: float, maximum_gap: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Return gap masses 0,...,maximum_gap-1 from survival factors p and s."""
    if not (0.0 < p < 1.0 and 0.0 < s < 1.0):
        raise ValueError("p and s must lie in (0,1)")
    if maximum_gap < 1:
        raise ValueError("maximum_gap must be positive")
    x = -math.log(p)
    y = -math.log(s)
    indices = np.arange(maximum_gap + 1, dtype=float)
    if math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14):
        rate = 0.5 * (x + y)
        survival = np.exp(-rate * indices) * (1.0 + rate * indices)
    else:
        survival = (y * p**indices - x * s**indices) / (y - x)
    return survival[:-1] - survival[1:]


def singular_gap_expansion(z: float, maximum_gap: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
    """Return g_z(k) and the d^2 coefficient for (p,s)=(z+d,z-d)."""
    if not 0.0 < z < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("z must lie in (0,1)")
    if maximum_gap < 1:
        raise ValueError("maximum_gap must be positive")
    k = np.arange(maximum_gap, dtype=float)
    log_z = math.log(z)
    denominator = 1.0 - z + log_z * (k * z - k + z)
    gap = z**k * denominator
    numerator = (
        k**3 * z * log_z
        - k**3 * log_z
        - 3.0 * k**2 * z
        + 3.0 * k**2 * log_z
        + 3.0 * k**2
        - 3.0 * k * z * log_z
        - 6.0 * k * z
        - 2.0 * z * log_z
        - 3.0 * z
    )
    coefficient = z**k * numerator / (6.0 * z**2)
    return gap, coefficient

"""Numerical feasibility checks for killed-reset D-MAP identifiability.

The serial model has a transient continuous-time generator with successive
rates ``rates``.  Sampling it at unit time gives T0=exp(Q); absorption is a
click and deterministically resets the next hidden state to the last phase,
so T1=(I-T0)1 e_n^T.  Its visible record is renewal.

This script checks six different questions that must not be conflated:

1. In the serial subclass, do visible coordinates recover the unordered rate
   multiset, including pole collisions?  A Hankel recurrence applied to the
   Palm gap-tail sequence recovers the sampled poles exp(-rate_i), with their
   algebraic multiplicities, for representative n=2,3,4 examples.
2. Does killed reset alone identify a hidden kernel?  No.  A stochastic
   similarity transform gives a different nonnegative killed-reset kernel
   with exactly the same visible renewal law.
3. Does a physical two-state inclusion triple satisfy the exact scalar image
   equation?  The residual is checked on separated and repeated-rate examples.
4. Does the hidden mode obey its sharp global secant-slope bound?
5. Does the exact mean sampled cycle have the stated small-interval expansion?
6. What is the complete Markovian similarity fibre of the physical two-state
   kernel?  The exact arc parameter runs between 1 and gamma/recovery; its
   endpoints are the rate-swapped physical kernels, while its interior is
   strictly positive and has the same complete Palm tail.

The numerical searches are evidence and diagnostics, not proofs of global
injectivity.  The associated manuscript theorem supplies the exact minimal
similarity-orbit criterion and proves serial identifiability for arbitrary
positive rates, including collision strata.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from numpy.typing import ArrayLike, NDArray
from scipy.linalg import eig, expm
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree


FloatArray = NDArray[np.float64]


def hidden_mode_secant(x: float, y: float) -> float:
    """Return the secant slope of t*exp(-t), with its diagonal limit."""
    if not np.isfinite(x) or not np.isfinite(y) or min(x, y) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("x and y must be finite and positive")
    if x == y:
        return float(np.exp(-x) * (1.0 - x))
    return float((y * np.exp(-y) - x * np.exp(-x)) / (y - x))


def symmetric_log_divided_difference(p: float, s: float) -> float:
    """Return the symmetric logarithmic divided difference C(p,s)."""
    if not np.isfinite(p) or not np.isfinite(s) or min(p, s) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("p and s must be finite and positive")
    midpoint = 0.5 * (p + s)
    half_gap = 0.5 * (p - s)
    if abs(half_gap) <= 1e-6 * midpoint:
        log_midpoint = np.log(midpoint)
        return float(
            midpoint * (1.0 - log_midpoint)
            + half_gap**2 / midpoint * (0.5 + log_midpoint / 3.0)
            + half_gap**4 / midpoint**3 * (1.0 / 12.0 + 4.0 * log_midpoint / 45.0)
        )
    return float((s * np.log(p) - p * np.log(s)) / (np.log(p) - np.log(s)))


def two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return (r0,r1,r2) for the physical two-state sampled counter."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    p = float(np.exp(-x))
    s = float(np.exp(-y))
    if x == y:
        b = x * p
    else:
        b = y * (p - s) / (y - x)
    a = 1.0 - s - b
    rho = (1.0 - p) * (1.0 - s) / (1.0 - p + b)
    hidden_lambda = p - b
    r1 = rho * a
    r2 = rho * rho + hidden_lambda * (r1 - rho * rho)
    return np.array([rho, r1, r2])


def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
    difference = recovery - gamma
    if difference == 0.0:
        b = recovery * delta * p
    else:
        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])


def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
    gamma: float, recovery: float
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
    finite_rates = np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery)))
    if not finite_rates or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
    endpoint = gamma / recovery
    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)


def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
    if not np.isfinite(q):
        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
    if q < lower or q > upper:
        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
    p = float(physical[0, 0])
    b = float(physical[1, 0])
    s = float(physical[1, 1])
    endpoint = gamma / recovery
    equivalent = np.array(
        [
            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
        ]
    )
    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
    return equivalent


def physical_image_residual(inclusions: ArrayLike) -> float:
    """Evaluate the exact three-inclusion sampled-counter image equation."""
    coordinates = np.asarray(inclusions, dtype=float)
    if coordinates.size != 3:
        raise ValueError("exactly r0, r1, and r2 are required")
    r0, r1, r2 = coordinates
    denominator = r1 - r0 * r0
    if r0 <= 0.0 or denominator == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("the inclusion triple is outside the stable inverse chart")
    a = r1 / r0
    hidden_lambda = (r2 - r0 * r0) / denominator
    sigma1 = 1.0 - a + hidden_lambda
    sigma2 = r0 * (1.0 - hidden_lambda) - a + hidden_lambda
    discriminant = sigma1 * sigma1 - 4.0 * sigma2
    if discriminant < -1e-13:
        raise ValueError("the quotient polynomial has nonreal roots")
    root_gap = np.sqrt(max(discriminant, 0.0))
    p = 0.5 * (sigma1 + root_gap)
    s = 0.5 * (sigma1 - root_gap)
    return float(a - 1.0 + symmetric_log_divided_difference(p, s))


def mean_cycle_length(gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float) -> float:
    """Return E(G+1) for the two-stage sampled cycle."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    gx = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-x))
    if x == y:
        return float(gx + x * np.exp(-x) * gx * gx)
    gy = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-y))
    return float((y * gx - x * gy) / (y - x))


def small_delta_mean_expansion(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> float:
    """Return the expansion of delta*E(G+1) through order delta^4."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    return float(
        1.0 / gamma
        + 1.0 / recovery
        + delta / 2.0
        + gamma * recovery * (gamma + recovery) * delta**4 / 720.0
    )


def serial_generator(rates: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the lower-bidiagonal transient generator for serial phases."""
    rate_array = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    scale = np.maximum(moments.std(axis=0), 1e-10)
    normalized = moments / scale
    distances, indices = cKDTree(normalized).query(normalized, k=2)
    index = int(np.argmin(distances[:, 1]))
    partner = int(indices[index, 1])
    moment_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(normalized[index] - normalized[partner]))
    rate_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(rates[index] - rates[partner]))
    return (
        moment_distance,
        rate_distance,
        tuple(rates[index]),
        tuple(rates[partner]),
    )


def array_string(values: ArrayLike) -> str:
    return np.array2string(
        np.asarray(values), precision=10, suppress_small=False, floatmode="fixed"
    )


def report_example(rates: tuple[float, ...], search_starts: int = 80) -> None:
    n_states = len(rates)
    t0, t1 = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
    tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 2 * n_states)
    extended_tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 3 * n_states + 1)
    moments = visible_click_moments(rates, 2 * n_states + 2)
    recurrence, recurrence_residual = recover_minimal_recurrence(
        extended_tails, n_states
    )
    roots = np.roots(recurrence)
    recovered_rates = np.sort(-np.log(np.abs(roots)))
    diagnostics = hankel_diagnostics(tails, n_states)
    permutations = list(itertools.permutations(rates))
    permutation_error = max(
        float(np.max(np.abs(visible_click_moments(item, 2 * n_states + 2) - moments)))
        for item in permutations
    )
    singular_values = np.linalg.svd(
        finite_difference_jacobian(rates, 2 * n_states + 2), compute_uv=False
    )

    print(f"n={n_states} serial killed-reset example")
    print(f"rates={rates}")
    print("T0=")
    print(array_string(t0))
    print("T1=")
    print(array_string(t1))
    print(f"Palm tails S_0,...,S_{2 * n_states - 1}={array_string(tails)}")
    print(f"click moments r_0,...,r_{2 * n_states + 2}={array_string(moments)}")
    print(f"Hankel recurrence polynomial={array_string(recurrence)}")
    print(f"expected sampled-pole polynomial={array_string(np.poly(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates))))}")
    print(f"maximum recurrence residual={recurrence_residual:.3e}")
    print(
        "leading Hankel diagnostics: "
        f"rank={diagnostics.rank}, determinant={diagnostics.determinant:.3e}, "
        f"condition={diagnostics.condition_number:.3e}, "
        f"sigma_min={diagnostics.smallest_singular_value:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"recovered unordered rates (root moduli)={array_string(recovered_rates)}")
    if n_states == 2:
        print(
            "three-inclusion recovered unordered rates="
            f"{array_string(recover_two_state_rates_from_three_inclusions(moments))}"
        )
    print(f"maximum moment error over all labelled permutations={permutation_error:.3e}")
    print(f"moment-map Jacobian singular values={array_string(singular_values)}")

    search = multistart_fiber_search(rates, starts=search_starts, seed=100 + n_states)
    print(
        f"multistart search: {search.converged}/{search.starts} converged; "
        f"canonical sorted fibers={search.canonical_fibers}"
    )
    print(f"labelled permutation orders reached={search.labelled_orders}")
    if np.isfinite(search.best_nonpermutation_residual):
        print(
            "WARNING: accepted non-permutation solution with scaled residual="
            f"{search.best_nonpermutation_residual:.3e}"
        )
    else:
        print("no accepted non-permutation solution found")

    nearest = random_nearest_pair_search(n_states, samples=900, seed=200 + n_states)
    print(
        "random nearest-pair search: normalized moment distance="
        f"{nearest[0]:.3e}, rate distance={nearest[1]:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"nearest sorted tuples={nearest[2]} and {nearest[3]}")

    equivalent = equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0, epsilon=0.02)
    tail_difference = float(
        np.max(
            np.abs(
                kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 20)
                - kernel_tail_coordinates(equivalent, 20)
            )
        )
    )
    print("non-serial stochastic-similarity equivalent T0'=")
    print(array_string(equivalent))
    print(f"||T0'-T0||_F={np.linalg.norm(equivalent - t0):.3e}")
    print(f"maximum S_0,...,S_19 difference={tail_difference:.3e}")
    print(f"reset-preserving similarity tangent dimension={(n_states - 1) ** 2}")
    print(
        "interpretation: killed reset alone has a nontrivial hidden-kernel "
        "fiber, while the serial rate tuple is recovered here only as an "
        "unordered multiset."
    )
    print()

 succeeded in 240ms:
# Feasibility note: n-state killed-reset D-MAP identifiability

## Decision

A universal labelled-kernel inverse is false, but a sharp minimal-class
dichotomy is attainable. Deterministic reset reduces the visible law to the
scalar Palm tail S_k = e_n^T K^k 1. Standard minimal realization theory says
that two rank-n representations of this sequence differ by a unique
similarity preserving 1 and e_n^T. Therefore a declared subclass is
identifiable, up to its allowed state relabellings, exactly when the
intersection of each such similarity orbit with the subclass's nonnegative
substochastic cone has one declared structural-equivalence class.

This orbit--cone criterion is necessary and sufficient, but its realization
input is established theory rather than a new general phase-type theorem.
The physical two-state orbit intersection can now be evaluated completely.
With \(q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), it is the closed arc generated by
\(M_q=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right]\) for
\(q\) between \(1\) and \(q_*\). Its endpoints
are the two rate-swapped physical kernels, all strict interior points are
positive nontriangular kernels, and the arc collapses to a singleton exactly
when the rates coincide. The other model-specific conclusions locate two
opposite higher-state classes:

- every minimal interior point of the unrestricted killed-reset cone has a
  continuum visible fibre;
- the pure serial absorption subclass identifies the unordered rate multiset
  for all positive rates, including repeated rates.

Pole collision is therefore not the identifiability boundary. In the serial
model it produces confluent Prony terms and singular finite-sample root
coordinates, while algebraic multiplicity still identifies the repeated rate
at population level. The boundary is the Markovian orbit fibre.

## Scope

The theorem assumes minimal/Hankel rank n. Lower-rank nominal n-state
representations require a separate stratified augmentation theory. For an
arbitrary fixed nonserial zero pattern, deciding the orbit--cone intersection
remains a graph-specific semialgebraic problem. These limitations are explicit
open interfaces in the manuscript.

## Machine evidence

verify_nstate_identifiability.py evaluates representative n=2,3,4 serial
models, including repeated sampled poles. It computes Palm tails and stationary
click moments, reconstructs the order-n Hankel recurrence, verifies full
Hankel rank, checks permutation invariance, runs deterministic fibre searches,
and constructs distinct reset-preserving similarity equivalents with identical
visible tails. It also evaluates the exact physical two-state fibre arc,
checks its swapped endpoints and strict interior positivity, and verifies full
Palm-tail invariance. The legacy aggregate output is
`artifacts/verify_nstate_identifiability_output.txt`; the new focused output is
`artifacts/verify_two_state_fibre_output.txt`.

Exact citations, arXiv API queries, DOI checks, and the restricted novelty
claim are recorded in artifacts/literature_check.md.

## Selected result

The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
paper's physical quotient story. For
\(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), every
reset-preserving similarity is generated by
\(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
Writing \(q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), the transformed upper-right entry
is \(b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q\). The lower-left entry forces \(q>0\), so Markov
nonnegativity is equivalent to \(q\) lying between \(1\) and \(q_*\). The two
endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates \(q_*=1\),
the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.
